50: struct WsStream {
51:     tx_command: mpsc::Sender<WsCommand>,
52:     rx_message: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Result<Message, WsError>>,
53:     pump_task: tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>,
54: }
55: 
56: enum WsCommand {
57:     Send {
58:         message: Message,
59:         tx_result: oneshot::Sender<Result<(), WsError>>,
60:     },
61: }
62: 
63: impl WsStream {
64:     fn new(inner: WebSocketConnection) -> Self {
65:         let (tx_command, mut rx_command) = mpsc::channel::<WsCommand>(32);
66:         let (tx_message, rx_message) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<Result<Message, WsError>>();
67: 
68:         let pump_task = tokio::spawn(async move {
69:             let mut inner = inner;
70:             loop {
71:                 tokio::select! {
72:                     command = rx_command.recv() => {
73:                         let Some(command) = command else {
74:                             break;
75:                         };
76:                         match command {
77:                             WsCommand::Send { message, tx_result } => {
78:                                 let result = inner.send(message).await;
79:                                 let should_break = result.is_err();
80:                                 let _ = tx_result.send(result);
81:                                 if should_break {
82:                                     break;
83:                                 }
84:                             }
85:                         }
86:                     }
87:                     message = inner.next() => {
88:                         let Some(message) = message else {
89:                             break;
90:                         };
91:                         match message {
92:                             Ok(Message::Ping(payload)) => {
93:                                 if let Err(err) = inner.send(Message::Pong(payload)).await {
94:                                     let _ = tx_message.send(Err(err));
95:                                     break;
96:                                 }
97:                             }
98:                             Ok(Message::Pong(_)) => {}
99:                             Ok(message @ (Message::Text(_)
100:                             | Message::Binary(_)
101:                             | Message::Close(_)
102:                             | Message::Frame(_))) => {
103:                                 let is_close = matches!(message, Message::Close(_));
104:                                 if tx_message.send(Ok(message)).is_err() {
105:                                     break;
106:                                 }
107:                                 if is_close {
108:                                     break;
109:                                 }
110:                             }
111:                             Err(err) => {
112:                                 let _ = tx_message.send(Err(err));
113:                                 break;
114:                             }
115:                         }
116:                     }
117:                 }
118:             }
119:         });
120: 
121:         Self {
122:             tx_command,
123:             rx_message,
124:             pump_task,
125:         }
126:     }
127: 
128:     async fn request(
129:         &self,
130:         make_command: impl FnOnce(oneshot::Sender<Result<(), WsError>>) -> WsCommand,
131:     ) -> Result<(), WsError> {
132:         let (tx_result, rx_result) = oneshot::channel();
133:         if self.tx_command.send(make_command(tx_result)).await.is_err() {
134:             return Err(WsError::ConnectionClosed);
135:         }
136:         rx_result.await.unwrap_or(Err(WsError::ConnectionClosed))
137:     }
138: 
139:     async fn send(&self, message: Message) -> Result<(), WsError> {
140:         self.request(|tx_result| WsCommand::Send { message, tx_result })
141:             .await
142:     }
143: 
144:     async fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Result<Message, WsError>> {
145:         self.rx_message.recv().await
146:     }
147: }
148: 
149: impl Drop for WsStream {
150:     fn drop(&mut self) {
151:         self.pump_task.abort();
152:     }
153: }

368:     pub reasoning_included: bool,
369:     /// Whether the server returned a server-selected model in the upgrade response.

375: impl ResponsesWebsocketClient {
376:     /// Creates a Responses WebSocket client for an already-resolved provider and auth source.
377:     pub fn new(provider: Provider, auth: SharedAuthProvider) -> Self {
378:         Self {
379:             provider,
380:             auth,
381:             endpoint: ResponsesEndpoint::Responses,
382:         }
383:     }
384: 
385:     /// Selects a Responses-compatible backend route for subsequent connections.
386:     pub fn with_endpoint(mut self, endpoint: ResponsesEndpoint) -> Self {
387:         self.endpoint = endpoint;
388:         self
389:     }
390: 
391:     #[instrument(
392:         name = "responses_websocket.connect",
393:         level = "info",
394:         skip_all,
395:         fields(transport = "responses_websocket", api.path = self.endpoint.path())
396:     )]
397:     pub async fn connect(
398:         &self,
399:         http_client_factory: &HttpClientFactory,
400:         extra_headers: HeaderMap,
401:         default_headers: HeaderMap,
402:         turn_state: Option<Arc<OnceLock<String>>>,
403:         telemetry: Option<Arc<dyn WebsocketTelemetry>>,
404:     ) -> Result<ResponsesWebsocketConnection, ApiError> {
405:         let ws_url = self
406:             .provider
407:             .websocket_url_for_path(self.endpoint.path())
408:             .map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to build websocket URL: {err}")))?;
409: 
410:         let mut headers =
411:             merge_request_headers(&self.provider.headers, extra_headers, default_headers);
412:         self.auth.add_auth_headers(&mut headers);
413: 
414:         let (stream, _status, server_reasoning_included, server_model) =
415:             connect_websocket(ws_url, headers, http_client_factory, turn_state.clone()).await?;
416:         Ok(ResponsesWebsocketConnection::new(
417:             stream,
418:             self.provider.stream_idle_timeout,
419:             server_reasoning_included,
420:             server_model,
421:             telemetry,
422:             self.endpoint,
423:         ))
424:     }
425: 
426:     /// Opens a WebSocket connection long enough to validate the upgrade response.
427:     ///
428:     /// The probe uses the same URL construction, headers, authentication, TLS,
429:     /// and custom-CA path as a real Responses WebSocket connection, but it does
430:     /// not send a request frame. After the HTTP 101 upgrade succeeds, it waits
431:     /// briefly for an immediate server close frame so diagnostics can distinguish
432:     /// a usable connection from a policy rejection that closes right away.
433:     pub async fn probe_handshake(
434:         &self,
435:         http_client_factory: &HttpClientFactory,
436:         extra_headers: HeaderMap,
437:         default_headers: HeaderMap,
438:         immediate_close_timeout: Duration,
439:     ) -> Result<ResponsesWebsocketProbe, ApiError> {
440:         let ws_url = self
441:             .provider
442:             .websocket_url_for_path(self.endpoint.path())
443:             .map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to build websocket URL: {err}")))?;
444: 
445:         let mut headers =
446:             merge_request_headers(&self.provider.headers, extra_headers, default_headers);
447:         self.auth.add_auth_headers(&mut headers);
448: 
449:         let (mut stream, status, reasoning_included, server_model) = connect_websocket(
450:             ws_url.clone(),
451:             headers,
452:             http_client_factory,
453:             /*turn_state*/ None,
454:         )
455:         .await?;
456:         let immediate_close = tokio::time::timeout(immediate_close_timeout, stream.next())
457:             .await
458:             .ok()
459:             .flatten()
460:             .transpose()
461:             .map_err(|err| {
462:                 ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to read websocket probe event: {err}"))
463:             })?
464:             .and_then(immediate_close_from_message);
465: 
466:         Ok(ResponsesWebsocketProbe {
467:             url: ws_url.to_string(),
468:             status,
469:             reasoning_included,
470:             server_model_present: server_model.is_some(),
471:             immediate_close,
472:         })
473:     }
474: }

476: fn immediate_close_from_message(message: Message) -> Option<ResponsesWebsocketClose> {
477:     let Message::Close(frame) = message else {
478:         return None;
479:     };
480:     frame.map(close_frame_to_probe)
481: }
482: 
483: fn close_frame_to_probe(frame: CloseFrame) -> ResponsesWebsocketClose {
484:     ResponsesWebsocketClose {
485:         code: frame.code.to_string(),
486:         reason: frame.reason.to_string(),
487:     }
488: }

490: fn merge_request_headers(
491:     provider_headers: &HeaderMap,
492:     extra_headers: HeaderMap,
493:     default_headers: HeaderMap,
494: ) -> HeaderMap {
495:     let mut headers = provider_headers.clone();
496:     headers.extend(extra_headers);
497:     for (name, value) in &default_headers {
498:         if let http::header::Entry::Vacant(entry) = headers.entry(name) {
499:             entry.insert(value.clone());
500:         }
501:     }
502:     headers
503: }

505: async fn connect_websocket(
506:     url: Url,
507:     headers: HeaderMap,
508:     http_client_factory: &HttpClientFactory,
509:     turn_state: Option<Arc<OnceLock<String>>>,
510: ) -> Result<(WsStream, StatusCode, bool, Option<String>), ApiError> {
511:     info!("connecting to websocket: {url}");
512: 
513:     let mut request = url
514:         .as_str()
515:         .into_client_request()
516:         .map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to build websocket request: {err}")))?;
517:     request.headers_mut().extend(headers);
518: 
519:     let connector = WebSocketConnector::new(http_client_factory)
520:         .map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to configure websocket TLS: {err}")))?;
521:     let response = connector.connect(request, websocket_config()).await;
522: 
523:     let (stream, response) = match response {
524:         Ok((stream, response)) => {
525:             info!(
526:                 "successfully connected to websocket: {url}, headers: {:?}",
527:                 response.headers()
528:             );
529:             (stream, response)
530:         }
531:         Err(err) => {
532:             error!("failed to connect to websocket: {err}, url: {url}");
533:             return Err(map_ws_error(err, &url));
534:         }
535:     };
536: 
537:     let reasoning_included = response.headers().contains_key(X_REASONING_INCLUDED_HEADER);
538:     let server_model = response
539:         .headers()
540:         .get(OPENAI_MODEL_HEADER)
541:         .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
542:         .map(ToString::to_string);
543:     if let Some(turn_state) = turn_state
544:         && let Some(header_value) = response
545:             .headers()
546:             .get(X_CODEX_TURN_STATE_HEADER)
547:             .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
548:     {
549:         let _ = turn_state.set(header_value.to_string());
550:     }
551:     Ok((
552:         WsStream::new(stream),
553:         response.status(),
554:         reasoning_included,
555:         server_model,
556:     ))
557: }

559: fn websocket_config() -> WebSocketConfig {
560:     let mut extensions = ExtensionsConfig::default();
561:     extensions.permessage_deflate = Some(DeflateConfig::default());
562: 
563:     let mut config = WebSocketConfig::default();
564:     config.extensions = extensions;
565:     config
566: }

568: fn map_ws_error(err: WsError, url: &Url) -> ApiError {
569:     match err {
570:         WsError::Http(response) => {
571:             let status = response.status();
572:             let headers = response.headers().clone();
573:             let body = response
574:                 .body()
575:                 .as_ref()
576:                 .and_then(|bytes| String::from_utf8(bytes.clone()).ok());
577:             ApiError::Transport(TransportError::Http {
578:                 status,
579:                 url: Some(url.to_string()),
580:                 headers: Some(headers),
581:                 body,
582:             })
583:         }
584:         WsError::ConnectionClosed | WsError::AlreadyClosed => {
585:             ApiError::Stream("websocket closed".to_string())
586:         }
587:         WsError::Io(err) => ApiError::Transport(TransportError::Network(err.to_string())),
588:         other => ApiError::Transport(TransportError::Network(other.to_string())),
589:     }
590: }

592: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
593: struct WrappedWebsocketError {
594:     code: Option<String>,
595:     message: Option<String>,
596: }
597: 
598: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
599: struct WrappedWebsocketErrorEvent {
600:     #[serde(rename = "type")]
601:     kind: String,
602:     #[serde(alias = "status_code")]
603:     status: Option<u16>,
604:     #[serde(default)]
605:     error: Option<WrappedWebsocketError>,
606:     #[serde(default)]
607:     headers: Option<JsonMap<String, Value>>,
608: }
609: 
610: fn parse_wrapped_websocket_error_event(payload: &str) -> Option<WrappedWebsocketErrorEvent> {
611:     let event: WrappedWebsocketErrorEvent = serde_json::from_str(payload).ok()?;
612:     if event.kind != "error" {
613:         return None;
614:     }
615:     Some(event)
616: }
617: 
618: fn map_wrapped_websocket_error_event(
619:     event: WrappedWebsocketErrorEvent,
620:     original_payload: String,
621: ) -> Option<ApiError> {
622:     let WrappedWebsocketErrorEvent {
623:         status,
624:         error,
625:         headers,
626:         ..
627:     } = event;
628: 
629:     if let Some(error) = error.as_ref()
630:         && let Some(code) = error.code.as_deref()
631:         && let Some(fallback_message) = match code {
632:             WEBSOCKET_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED_CODE => {
633:                 Some(WEBSOCKET_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED_MESSAGE)
634:             }
635:             PREVIOUS_RESPONSE_NOT_FOUND_CODE => Some(PREVIOUS_RESPONSE_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE),
636:             _ => None,
637:         }
638:     {
639:         return Some(ApiError::Retryable {
640:             message: error
641:                 .message
642:                 .clone()
643:                 .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback_message.to_string()),
644:             delay: None,
645:         });
646:     }
647: 
648:     let status = StatusCode::from_u16(status?).ok()?;
649:     if status.is_success() {
650:         return None;
651:     }
652: 
653:     Some(ApiError::Transport(TransportError::Http {
654:         status,
655:         url: None,
656:         headers: headers.as_ref().map(json_headers_to_http_headers),
657:         body: Some(original_payload),
658:     }))
659: }
660: 
661: fn json_headers_to_http_headers(headers: &JsonMap<String, Value>) -> HeaderMap {
662:     let mut mapped = HeaderMap::new();
663:     for (name, value) in headers {
664:         let Ok(header_name) = HeaderName::from_bytes(name.as_bytes()) else {
665:             continue;
666:         };
667:         let Some(header_value) = json_header_value(value) else {
668:             continue;
669:         };
670:         mapped.insert(header_name, header_value);
671:     }
672:     mapped
673: }
674: 
675: fn json_header_value(value: &Value) -> Option<HeaderValue> {
676:     let value = match value {
677:         Value::String(value) => value.clone(),
678:         Value::Number(value) => value.to_string(),
679:         Value::Bool(value) => value.to_string(),
680:         _ => return None,
681:     };
682:     HeaderValue::from_str(&value).ok()
683: }

685: async fn run_websocket_response_stream(
686:     ws_stream: &mut WsStream,
687:     tx_event: mpsc::Sender<std::result::Result<ResponseEvent, ApiError>>,
688:     request_text: String,
689:     idle_timeout: Duration,
690:     telemetry: Option<Arc<dyn WebsocketTelemetry>>,
691:     turn_state: Option<&OnceLock<String>>,
692:     timing_log_context: &ResponsesWebsocketTimingLogContext,
693: ) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
694:     let mut last_server_model: Option<String> = None;
695:     let mut safety_buffering_treatment = SafetyBufferingTreatment::default();
696:     send_websocket_request(
697:         ws_stream,
698:         request_text,
699:         idle_timeout,
700:         telemetry.as_ref(),
701:         timing_log_context.connection_reused,
702:     )
703:     .await?;
704: 
705:     loop {
706:         let poll_start = Instant::now();
707:         let response = tokio::time::timeout(idle_timeout, ws_stream.next())
708:             .await
709:             .map_err(|_| ApiError::Stream("idle timeout waiting for websocket".into()));
710:         if let Some(t) = telemetry.as_ref() {
711:             t.on_ws_event(&response, poll_start.elapsed());
712:         }
713:         let message = match response {
714:             Ok(Some(Ok(msg))) => msg,
715:             Ok(Some(Err(err))) => {
716:                 return Err(ApiError::Stream(err.to_string()));
717:             }
718:             Ok(None) => {
719:                 return Err(ApiError::Stream(
720:                     "stream closed before response.completed".into(),
721:                 ));
722:             }
723:             Err(err) => {
724:                 return Err(err);
725:             }
726:         };
727: 
728:         match message {
729:             Message::Text(text) => {
730:                 if let Some(wrapped_error) = parse_wrapped_websocket_error_event(&text)
731:                     && let Some(error) =
732:                         map_wrapped_websocket_error_event(wrapped_error, text.to_string())
733:                 {
734:                     return Err(error);
735:                 }
736: 
737:                 let event = match serde_json::from_str::<ResponsesStreamEvent>(&text) {
738:                     Ok(event) => event,
739:                     Err(err) => {
740:                         debug!("failed to parse websocket event: {err}, data: {text}");
741:                         continue;
742:                     }
743:                 };
744:                 emit_responses_websocket_timing_event(
745:                     event.kind(),
746:                     text.as_str(),
747:                     timing_log_context,
748:                 );
749:                 if event.kind() == "codex.response.metadata"
750:                     && let Some(etag) =
751:                         event
752:                             .headers
753:                             .as_ref()
754:                             .and_then(Value::as_object)
755:                             .and_then(|headers| {
756:                                 json_headers_to_http_headers(headers)
757:                                     .get(X_MODELS_ETAG_HEADER)
758:                                     .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
759:                                     .map(str::to_string)
760:                             })
761:                 {
762:                     let _ = tx_event.send(Ok(ResponseEvent::ModelsEtag(etag))).await;
763:                 }
764:                 if let Some(response_turn_state) = event.turn_state()
765:                     && let Some(turn_state) = turn_state
766:                 {
767:                     let _ = turn_state.set(response_turn_state);
768:                 }
769:                 let model_verifications = event.model_verifications();
770:                 let turn_moderation_metadata = event.turn_moderation_metadata();
771:                 let safety_buffering =
772:                     safety_buffering_for_event(&event, &mut safety_buffering_treatment);
773:                 if event.kind() == "codex.rate_limits" {
774:                     if let Some(snapshot) = parse_rate_limit_event(&text) {
775:                         let _ = tx_event.send(Ok(ResponseEvent::RateLimits(snapshot))).await;
776:                     }
777:                     continue;
778:                 }
779:                 if let Some(model) = event.response_model()
780:                     && last_server_model.as_deref() != Some(model.as_str())
781:                 {
782:                     let _ = tx_event
783:                         .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::ServerModel(model.clone())))
784:                         .await;
785:                     last_server_model = Some(model);
786:                 }
787:                 if let Some(verifications) = model_verifications
788:                     && tx_event
789:                         .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::ModelVerifications(verifications)))
790:                         .await
791:                         .is_err()
792:                 {
793:                     return Err(ApiError::Stream(
794:                         "response event consumer dropped".to_string(),
795:                     ));
796:                 }
797:                 if let Some(metadata) = turn_moderation_metadata
798:                     && tx_event
799:                         .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::TurnModerationMetadata(metadata)))
800:                         .await
801:                         .is_err()
802:                 {
803:                     return Err(ApiError::Stream(
804:                         "response event consumer dropped".to_string(),
805:                     ));
806:                 }
807:                 if let Some(buffering) = safety_buffering
808:                     && tx_event
809:                         .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::SafetyBuffering(buffering)))
810:                         .await
811:                         .is_err()
812:                 {
813:                     return Err(ApiError::Stream(
814:                         "response event consumer dropped".to_string(),
815:                     ));
816:                 }
817:                 match process_responses_event(event) {
818:                     Ok(Some(event)) => {
819:                         let is_completed = matches!(event, ResponseEvent::Completed { .. });
820:                         let _ = tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await;
821:                         if is_completed {
822:                             break;
823:                         }
824:                     }
825:                     Ok(None) => {}
826:                     Err(error) => {
827:                         return Err(error.into_api_error());
828:                     }
829:                 }
830:             }
831:             Message::Binary(_) => {
832:                 return Err(ApiError::Stream("unexpected binary websocket event".into()));
833:             }
834:             Message::Close(_) => {
835:                 return Err(ApiError::Stream(
836:                     "websocket closed by server before response.completed".into(),
837:                 ));
838:             }
839:             Message::Frame(_) => {}
840:             Message::Ping(_) | Message::Pong(_) => {}
841:         }
842:     }
843: 
844:     Ok(())
845: }

847: fn emit_responses_websocket_timing_event(
848:     kind: &str,
849:     payload: &str,
850:     context: &ResponsesWebsocketTimingLogContext,
851: ) {
852:     if kind != RESPONSES_WEBSOCKET_TIMING_KIND {
853:         return;
854:     }
855: 
856:     // This full payload is excluded from always-on sinks. Opt in with
857:     // `RUST_LOG='codex_api::responses_websocket_timing=trace'`.
858:     tracing::event!(
859:         name: RESPONSES_WEBSOCKET_TIMING_KIND,
860:         target: RESPONSES_WEBSOCKET_TIMING_EVENT_TARGET,
861:         tracing::Level::TRACE,
862:         model = context.model.as_str(),
863:         session_id = context.session_id.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),
864:         thread_id = context.thread_id.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),
865:         turn_id = context.turn_id.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),
866:         traceparent = context.traceparent.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),
867:         previous_response_id = context.previous_response_id.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),
868:         request_start_ms = context.request_start_ms.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),
869:         warmup = context.warmup,
870:         connection_reused = context.connection_reused,
871:         payload,
872:         "responses websocket timing"
873:     );
874: }

876: fn safety_buffering_for_event(
877:     event: &ResponsesStreamEvent,
878:     treatment: &mut SafetyBufferingTreatment,
879: ) -> Option<crate::common::SafetyBuffering> {
880:     if let Some(headers) = event.headers.as_ref().and_then(Value::as_object)
881:         && let Some(updated_treatment) =
882:             treatment_from_headers(&json_headers_to_http_headers(headers))
883:     {
884:         *treatment = updated_treatment;
885:     }
886:     event.safety_buffering(treatment)
887: }

889: async fn send_websocket_request(
890:     ws_stream: &WsStream,
891:     request_text: String,
892:     idle_timeout: Duration,
893:     telemetry: Option<&Arc<dyn WebsocketTelemetry>>,
894:     connection_reused: bool,
895: ) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
896:     let request_start = Instant::now();
897:     let result = tokio::time::timeout(
898:         idle_timeout,
899:         ws_stream.send(Message::Text(request_text.into())),
900:     )
901:     .await
902:     .map_err(|_| ApiError::Stream("idle timeout sending websocket request".into()))
903:     .and_then(|result| {
904:         result.map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to send websocket request: {err}")))
905:     });
906: 
907:     if let Some(t) = telemetry.as_ref() {
908:         t.on_ws_request(
909:             request_start.elapsed(),
910:             result.as_ref().err(),
911:             connection_reused,
912:         );
913:     }
914: 
915:     result?;
916: 
917:     Ok(())
918: }

921:     serde_json::to_string(request)
922:         .map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to encode websocket request: {err}")))
923: }

## The `codex-core` crate

Over time, the `codex-core` crate (defined in `codex-rs/core/`) has become bloated because it is the largest crate, so it is often easier to add something new to `codex-core` rather than refactor out the library code you need so your new code neither takes a dependency on, nor contributes to the size of, `codex-core`.

To that end: **resist adding code to codex-core**!

Particularly when introducing a new concept/feature/API, before adding to `codex-core`, consider whether:

- There is an existing crate other than `codex-core` that is an appropriate place for your new code to live.
- It is time to introduce a new crate to the Cargo workspace for your new functionality. Refactor existing code as necessary to make this happen.

Likewise, when reviewing code, do not hesitate to push back on PRs that would unnecessarily add code to `codex-core`.

## Code Review Rules

### Crate API surface

Keep crate API surfaces as small as possible. Avoid proliferating test-only helpers.

### Model visible context

Suffice maintains a context (history of messages) that is sent to the model in inference requests.

1. No history rewrite - the context must be built up incrementally.
2. Avoid frequent changes to context that cause cache misses.
3. No unbounded items - everything injected in the model context must have a bounded size and a hard cap.
4. No items larger than 10K tokens.
5. Highlight new individual items that can cross >1k tokens as P0. These need an additional manual review.
6. All injected fragments must be defined as structs in `core/context` and implement ContextualUserFragment trait

### Breaking changes

Search for breaking changes in external integration surfaces:

- app-server APIs
- raw response item events (`rawResponseItem/*`), even while experimental
- CLI parameters
- configuration loading
- resuming sessions from existing rollouts

### Test authoring guidance

For agent changes prefer integration tests over unit tests. Integration tests are under `core/suite` and use `test_codex` to set up a test instance of codex.

Features that change the agent logic MUST add an integration test:

- Provide a list of major logic changes and user-facing behaviors that need to be tested.

If unit tests are needed, put them in a dedicated test file (\*\_tests.rs).
Avoid test-only functions in the main implementation.

Check whether there are existing helpers to make tests more streamlined and readable.

### Change size guidance (800 lines)

Unless the change is mechanical the total number of changed lines should not exceed 800 lines.
For complex logic changes the size should be under 500 lines.

If the change is larger, explore whether it can be split into reviewable stages and identify the smallest coherent stage to land first.
Base the staging suggestion on the actual diff, dependencies, and affected call sites.

## TUI style conventions

## TUI code conventions

- Use concise styling helpers from ratatui’s Stylize trait.
  - Basic spans: use "text".into()
  - Styled spans: use "text".red(), "text".green(), "text".magenta(), "text".dim(), etc.
  - Prefer these over constructing styles with `Span::styled` and `Style` directly.
  - Example: patch summary file lines
    - Desired: vec!["  └ ".into(), "M".red(), " ".dim(), "tui/src/app.rs".dim()]

### TUI Styling (ratatui)

- Prefer Stylize helpers: use "text".dim(), .bold(), .cyan(), .italic(), .underlined() instead of manual Style where possible.
- Prefer simple conversions: use "text".into() for spans and vec![…].into() for lines; when inference is ambiguous (e.g., Paragraph::new/Cell::from), use Line::from(spans) or Span::from(text).
- Computed styles: if the Style is computed at runtime, using `Span::styled` is OK (`Span::from(text).set_style(style)` is also acceptable).
- Avoid hardcoded white: do not use `.white()`; prefer the default foreground (no color).
- Chaining: combine helpers by chaining for readability (e.g., url.cyan().underlined()).
- Single items: prefer "text".into(); use Line::from(text) or Span::from(text) only when the target type isn’t obvious from context, or when using .into() would require extra type annotations.
- Building lines: use vec![…].into() to construct a Line when the target type is obvious and no extra type annotations are needed; otherwise use Line::from(vec![…]).
- Avoid churn: don’t refactor between equivalent forms (Span::styled ↔ set_style, Line::from ↔ .into()) without a clear readability or functional gain; follow file‑local conventions and do not introduce type annotations solely to satisfy .into().
- Compactness: prefer the form that stays on one line after rustfmt; if only one of Line::from(vec![…]) or vec![…].into() avoids wrapping, choose that. If both wrap, pick the one with fewer wrapped lines.

### Text wrapping

- Always use textwrap::wrap to wrap plain strings.
- If you have a ratatui Line and you want to wrap it, use the helpers in tui/src/wrapping.rs, e.g. word_wrap_lines / word_wrap_line.
- If you need to indent wrapped lines, use the initial_indent / subsequent_indent options from RtOptions if you can, rather than writing custom logic.
- If you have a list of lines and you need to prefix them all with some prefix (optionally different on the first vs subsequent lines), use the `prefix_lines` helper from line_utils.

- Use an explicit `#[path = "..._tests.rs"]` attribute so the test filename is descriptive and easy to locate:

This repo uses snapshot tests (via `insta`), especially in `codex-rs/tui`, to validate rendered output.

When UI or text output changes intentionally, update the snapshots as follows:

### Test assertions

## App-server API Development Best Practices

These guidelines apply to app-server protocol work in `codex-rs`, especially:

- `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`
- `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2.rs`
- `app-server/README.md`

### Core Rules

- All active API development should happen in app-server v2. Do not add new API surface area to v1.
- Follow payload naming consistently:
  `*Params` for request payloads, `*Response` for responses, and `*Notification` for notifications.
- Expose RPC methods as `<resource>/<method>` and keep `<resource>` singular (for example, `thread/read`, `app/list`).
- Always expose fields as camelCase on the wire with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` unless a tagged union or explicit compatibility requirement needs a targeted rename.
- Always expose string enum values as camelCase on the wire with matching serde and TS `rename_all = "camelCase"` annotations unless an explicit compatibility requirement needs targeted renames.
- Exception: config RPC payloads are expected to use snake_case to mirror config.toml keys (see the config read/write/list APIs in `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2.rs`).
- Always set `#[ts(export_to = "v2/")]` on v2 request/response/notification types so generated TypeScript lands in the correct namespace.
- Never use `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` for v2 API payload fields.
  Exception: client->server requests that intentionally have no params may use:
  `params: #[ts(type = "undefined")] #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] Option<()>`.
- Keep Rust and TS wire renames aligned. If a field or variant uses `#[serde(rename = "...")]`, add matching `#[ts(rename = "...")]`.
- For discriminated unions, use explicit tagging in both serializers:
  `#[serde(tag = "type", ...)]` and `#[ts(tag = "type", ...)]`.
- Prefer plain `String` IDs at the API boundary (do UUID parsing/conversion internally if needed).
- Timestamps should be integer Unix seconds (`i64`) and named `*_at` (for example, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `resets_at`).
- For experimental API surface area:
  use `#[experimental("method/or/field")]`, derive `ExperimentalApi` when field-level gating is needed, and use `inspect_params: true` in `common.rs` when only some fields of a method are experimental.

### Client->server request payloads (`*Params`)

- Every optional field must be annotated with `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`. Do not use `#[ts(optional = nullable)]` outside client->server request payloads (`*Params`).
- Optional collection fields (for example `Vec`, `HashMap`) must use `Option<...>` + `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`. Do not use `#[serde(default)]` to model optional collections, and do not use `skip_serializing_if` on v2 payload fields.
- When you want omission to mean `false` for boolean fields, use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")] pub field: bool` over `Option<bool>`.
- For new list methods, implement cursor pagination by default:
  request fields `pub cursor: Option<String>` and `pub limit: Option<u32>`,
  response fields `pub data: Vec<...>` and `pub next_cursor: Option<String>`.

### Development Workflow

- Update app-server docs/examples when API behavior changes (at minimum `app-server/README.md`).
- Regenerate schema fixtures when API shapes change:
  `just write-app-server-schema`
  (and `just write-app-server-schema --experimental` when experimental API fixtures are affected).
- Validate with `just test -p codex-app-server-protocol`.
- Avoid boilerplate tests that only assert experimental field markers for individual
  request fields in `common.rs`; rely on schema generation/tests and behavioral coverage instead.

## Python Development Best Practices

### Ignore Python 2 compatibility

This project uses Python 3+. You should not use the `__future__` module.

If you need to worry about feature compatibility between different 3.xx point releases, check the
closest `pyproject.toml`'s `requires-python` field to see what minimum runtime version is supported.

## Platform Support

Tests and features must support Linux, macOS and Windows unless feature is explicitly OS-specific.

Suffice supports running connected app-server and exec-server on different operating systems. See the
`$remote-tests` skill for details about integration testing these configurations.

# Rust/codex-rs

In the codex-rs folder where the rust code lives:

- Crate names are prefixed with `codex-`. For example, the `core` folder's crate is named `codex-core`
- When using format! and you can inline variables into {}, always do that.
- Install any commands the repo relies on (for example `just`, `rg`, or `cargo-insta`) if they aren't already available before running instructions here.
- Never add or modify any code related to `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED_ENV_VAR` or `CODEX_SANDBOX_ENV_VAR`.
  - You operate in a sandbox where `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1` will be set whenever you use the `shell` tool. Any existing code that uses `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED_ENV_VAR` was authored with this fact in mind. It is often used to early exit out of tests that the author knew you would not be able to run given your sandbox limitations.
  - Similarly, when you spawn a process using Seatbelt (`/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`), `CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt` will be set on the child process. Integration tests that want to run Seatbelt themselves cannot be run under Seatbelt, so checks for `CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt` are also often used to early exit out of tests, as appropriate.
- Always collapse if statements per https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/index.html#collapsible_if
- Always inline format! args when possible per https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/index.html#uninlined_format_args
- Use method references over closures when possible per https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/index.html#redundant_closure_for_method_calls
- Avoid bool or ambiguous `Option` parameters that force callers to write hard-to-read code such as `foo(false)` or `bar(None)`. Prefer enums, named methods, newtypes, or other idiomatic Rust API shapes when they keep the callsite self-documenting.
- When you cannot make that API change and still need a small positional-literal callsite in Rust, follow the `argument_comment_lint` convention:
  - Use an exact `/*param_name*/` comment before opaque literal arguments such as `None`, booleans, and numeric literals when passing them by position.
  - A method's sole non-self argument is exempt when the method and parameter names match, such as `.enabled(false)` for `fn enabled(&self, enabled: bool)`.
  - Do not add these comments for string or char literals unless the comment adds real clarity; those literals are intentionally exempt from the lint.
  - The parameter name in the comment must exactly match the callee signature.
  - You can run `just argument-comment-lint` to run the lint check locally. This is powered by Bazel, so running it the first time can be slow if Bazel is not warmed up, though incremental invocations should take <15s. Most of the time, it is best to update the PR and let CI take responsibility for checking this (or run it asynchronously in the background after submitting the PR). Note CI checks all three platforms, which the local run does not.
- When possible, make `match` statements exhaustive and avoid wildcard arms.
- Newly added traits should include doc comments that explain their role and how implementations are expected to use them.
- Discourage both `#[async_trait]` and `#[allow(async_fn_in_trait)]` in Rust traits.
  - Prefer native RPITIT trait methods with explicit `Send` bounds on the returned future, as in `3c7f013f9735` / `#16630`.
  - Preferred trait shape:
    `fn foo(&self, ...) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = T> + Send;`
  - Implementations may still use `async fn foo(&self, ...) -> T` when they satisfy that contract.
  - Do not use `#[allow(async_fn_in_trait)]` as a shortcut around spelling the future contract explicitly.
- When writing tests, prefer comparing the equality of entire objects over fields one by one.
- Do not add tests for values that are statically defined.
- Do not add negative tests for logic that was removed.
- Do not add general product or user-facing documentation to the `docs/` folder. The official Suffice documentation lives elsewhere. The exception is app-server API documentation, which is covered by the app-server guidance below.
- Prefer private modules and explicitly exported public crate API.
- If you change `ConfigToml` or nested config types, run `just write-config-schema` to update `codex-rs/core/config.schema.json`.
- When working with MCP tool calls, prefer using `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/mcp_connection_manager.rs` to handle mutation of tools and tool calls. Aim to minimize the footprint of changes and leverage existing abstractions rather than plumbing code through multiple levels of function calls.
- Do not call `reset_client_session` unnecessarily; let the incremental check logic decide whether to reuse the previous request.
- If you change Rust dependencies (`Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`), run `just bazel-lock-update` from the
  repo root to refresh `MODULE.bazel.lock`, and include that lockfile update in the same change. CI
  verifies lockfile drift.
- Bazel does not automatically make source-tree files available to compile-time Rust file access. If
  you add `include_str!`, `include_bytes!`, `sqlx::migrate!`, or similar build-time file or
  directory reads, update the crate's `BUILD.bazel` (`compile_data`, `build_script_data`, or test
  data) or Bazel may fail even when Cargo passes.
- Do not create small helper methods that are referenced only once.
- For tracing async work, instrument the function or method definition with
  `#[tracing::instrument(...)]` instead of attaching spans to futures with
  `.instrument(...)` at call sites. Before adding instrumentation, check whether the callee—or
  the implementation method it immediately delegates to—is already instrumented.
- Avoid large modules:
  - Prefer adding new modules instead of growing existing ones.
  - Target Rust modules under 500 LoC, excluding tests.
  - If a file exceeds roughly 800 LoC, add new functionality in a new module instead of extending
    the existing file unless there is a strong documented reason not to.
  - This rule applies especially to high-touch files that already attract unrelated changes, such
    as `codex-rs/tui/src/app.rs`, `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/chat_composer.rs`,
    `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/footer.rs`, `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs`,
    `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/mod.rs`, and similarly central orchestration modules.
  - When extracting code from a large module, move the related tests and module/type docs toward
    the new implementation so the invariants stay close to the code that owns them.
  - Avoid adding new standalone methods to `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs` unless the change is
    trivial; prefer new modules/files and keep `chatwidget.rs` focused on orchestration.
- When running Rust commands (e.g. `just fix` or `just test`) be patient with the command and never try to kill them using the PID. Rust lock can make the execution slow, this is expected.

Run `just fmt` (in the `codex-rs` directory) automatically after you have finished making code changes anywhere in this repository; do not ask for approval to run it. Additionally, run the tests:

1. Do not run `cargo test` directly. Use `just test` so test execution follows the repo defaults.
2. Run the test for the specific project that was changed. For example, if changes were made in `codex-rs/tui`, run `just test -p codex-tui`.
3. Once those pass, if any changes were made in common, core, or protocol, run the complete test suite with `just test`. Avoid `--all-features` for routine local runs because it expands the build matrix and can significantly increase `target/` disk usage; use it only when you specifically need full feature coverage. project-specific or individual tests can be run without asking the user, but do ask the user before running the complete test suite.

Before finalizing a large change to `codex-rs`, run `just fix -p <project>` (in `codex-rs` directory) to fix any linter issues in the code. Prefer scoping with `-p` to avoid slow workspace‑wide Clippy builds; only run `just fix` without `-p` if you changed shared crates. Do not re-run tests after running `fix` or `fmt`.

## The `codex-core` crate

Over time, the `codex-core` crate (defined in `codex-rs/core/`) has become bloated because it is the largest crate, so it is often easier to add something new to `codex-core` rather than refactor out the library code you need so your new code neither takes a dependency on, nor contributes to the size of, `codex-core`.

To that end: **resist adding code to codex-core**!

Particularly when introducing a new concept/feature/API, before adding to `codex-core`, consider whether:

- There is an existing crate other than `codex-core` that is an appropriate place for your new code to live.
- It is time to introduce a new crate to the Cargo workspace for your new functionality. Refactor existing code as necessary to make this happen.

Likewise, when reviewing code, do not hesitate to push back on PRs that would unnecessarily add code to `codex-core`.

## Code Review Rules

### Crate API surface

Keep crate API surfaces as small as possible. Avoid proliferating test-only helpers.

### Model visible context

Suffice maintains a context (history of messages) that is sent to the model in inference requests.

1. No history rewrite - the context must be built up incrementally.
2. Avoid frequent changes to context that cause cache misses.
3. No unbounded items - everything injected in the model context must have a bounded size and a hard cap.
4. No items larger than 10K tokens.
5. Highlight new individual items that can cross >1k tokens as P0. These need an additional manual review.
6. All injected fragments must be defined as structs in `core/context` and implement ContextualUserFragment trait

### Breaking changes

Search for breaking changes in external integration surfaces:

- app-server APIs
- raw response item events (`rawResponseItem/*`), even while experimental
- CLI parameters
- configuration loading
- resuming sessions from existing rollouts

### Test authoring guidance

For agent changes prefer integration tests over unit tests. Integration tests are under `core/suite` and use `test_codex` to set up a test instance of codex.

Features that change the agent logic MUST add an integration test:

- Provide a list of major logic changes and user-facing behaviors that need to be tested.

If unit tests are needed, put them in a dedicated test file (\*\_tests.rs).
Avoid test-only functions in the main implementation.

Check whether there are existing helpers to make tests more streamlined and readable.

### Change size guidance (800 lines)

Unless the change is mechanical the total number of changed lines should not exceed 800 lines.
For complex logic changes the size should be under 500 lines.

If the change is larger, explore whether it can be split into reviewable stages and identify the smallest coherent stage to land first.
Base the staging suggestion on the actual diff, dependencies, and affected call sites.

## TUI style conventions

See `codex-rs/tui/styles.md`.

## TUI code conventions

- Use concise styling helpers from ratatui’s Stylize trait.
  - Basic spans: use "text".into()
  - Styled spans: use "text".red(), "text".green(), "text".magenta(), "text".dim(), etc.
  - Prefer these over constructing styles with `Span::styled` and `Style` directly.
  - Example: patch summary file lines
    - Desired: vec!["  └ ".into(), "M".red(), " ".dim(), "tui/src/app.rs".dim()]

### TUI Styling (ratatui)

- Prefer Stylize helpers: use "text".dim(), .bold(), .cyan(), .italic(), .underlined() instead of manual Style where possible.
- Prefer simple conversions: use "text".into() for spans and vec![…].into() for lines; when inference is ambiguous (e.g., Paragraph::new/Cell::from), use Line::from(spans) or Span::from(text).
- Computed styles: if the Style is computed at runtime, using `Span::styled` is OK (`Span::from(text).set_style(style)` is also acceptable).
- Avoid hardcoded white: do not use `.white()`; prefer the default foreground (no color).
- Chaining: combine helpers by chaining for readability (e.g., url.cyan().underlined()).
- Single items: prefer "text".into(); use Line::from(text) or Span::from(text) only when the target type isn’t obvious from context, or when using .into() would require extra type annotations.
- Building lines: use vec![…].into() to construct a Line when the target type is obvious and no extra type annotations are needed; otherwise use Line::from(vec![…]).
- Avoid churn: don’t refactor between equivalent forms (Span::styled ↔ set_style, Line::from ↔ .into()) without a clear readability or functional gain; follow file‑local conventions and do not introduce type annotations solely to satisfy .into().
- Compactness: prefer the form that stays on one line after rustfmt; if only one of Line::from(vec![…]) or vec![…].into() avoids wrapping, choose that. If both wrap, pick the one with fewer wrapped lines.

### Text wrapping

- Always use textwrap::wrap to wrap plain strings.
- If you have a ratatui Line and you want to wrap it, use the helpers in tui/src/wrapping.rs, e.g. word_wrap_lines / word_wrap_line.
- If you need to indent wrapped lines, use the initial_indent / subsequent_indent options from RtOptions if you can, rather than writing custom logic.
- If you have a list of lines and you need to prefix them all with some prefix (optionally different on the first vs subsequent lines), use the `prefix_lines` helper from line_utils.

## Tests

### Test module organization

- When adding a new test module, define its contents in a separate sibling file rather than inline in the implementation file.
- Use an explicit `#[path = "..._tests.rs"]` attribute so the test filename is descriptive and easy to locate:

  ```rust
  #[cfg(test)]
  #[path = "parser_tests.rs"]
  mod tests;
  ```

- This applies only when introducing a new test module. Do not move or rewrite existing inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` modules solely to follow this convention.

### Snapshot tests

This repo uses snapshot tests (via `insta`), especially in `codex-rs/tui`, to validate rendered output.

**Requirement:** any change that affects user-visible UI (including adding new UI) must include
corresponding `insta` snapshot coverage (add a new snapshot test if one doesn't exist yet, or
update the existing snapshot). Review and accept snapshot updates as part of the PR so UI impact
is easy to review and future diffs stay visual.

When UI or text output changes intentionally, update the snapshots as follows:

- Run tests to generate any updated snapshots:
  - `just test -p codex-tui`
- Check what’s pending:
  - `cargo insta pending-snapshots -p codex-tui`
- Review changes by reading the generated `*.snap.new` files directly in the repo, or preview a specific file:
  - `cargo insta show -p codex-tui path/to/file.snap.new`
- Only if you intend to accept all new snapshots in this crate, run:
  - `cargo insta accept -p codex-tui`

If you don’t have the tool:

- `cargo install --locked cargo-insta`

### Benchmarks

cargo benchmarks can be run with `just bench`, use the divan crate to write new ones.

Use `just bench-smoke` to dry-run the benchmark for a single iteration to ensure it works.

### Test assertions

- Tests should use pretty_assertions::assert_eq for clearer diffs. Import this at the top of the test module if it isn't already.
- Prefer deep equals comparisons whenever possible. Perform `assert_eq!()` on entire objects, rather than individual fields.
- Avoid mutating process environment in tests; prefer passing environment-derived flags or dependencies from above.

### Spawning workspace binaries in tests (Cargo vs Bazel)

- Prefer `codex_utils_cargo_bin::cargo_bin("...")` over `assert_cmd::Command::cargo_bin(...)` or `escargot` when tests need to spawn first-party binaries.
  - Under Bazel, binaries and resources may live under runfiles; use `codex_utils_cargo_bin::cargo_bin` to resolve absolute paths that remain stable after `chdir`.
- When locating fixture files or test resources under Bazel, avoid `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`. Prefer `codex_utils_cargo_bin::find_resource!` so paths resolve correctly under both Cargo and Bazel runfiles.

### Integration tests

#### codex_core integration testing

- Prefer the utilities in `core_test_support::responses` when writing end-to-end Suffice tests.
- Use `TestCodexBuilder::build_with_auto_env()` by default to ensure that new tests work with
  foreign app/exec OSes. See $remote-tests for details.
- All `mount_sse*` helpers return a `ResponseMock`; hold onto it so you can assert against outbound `/responses` POST bodies.
- Use `ResponseMock::single_request()` when a test should only issue one POST, or `ResponseMock::requests()` to inspect every captured `ResponsesRequest`.
- `ResponsesRequest` exposes helpers (`body_json`, `input`, `function_call_output`, `custom_tool_call_output`, `call_output`, `header`, `path`, `query_param`) so assertions can target structured payloads instead of manual JSON digging.
- Build SSE payloads with the provided `ev_*` constructors and the `sse(...)`.
- Prefer `wait_for_event` over `wait_for_event_with_timeout`.
- Prefer `mount_sse_once` over `mount_sse_once_match` or `mount_sse_sequence`

- Typical pattern:

  ```rust
  let mock = responses::mount_sse_once(&server, responses::sse(vec![
      responses::ev_response_created("resp-1"),
      responses::ev_function_call(call_id, "shell", &serde_json::to_string(&args)?),
      responses::ev_completed("resp-1"),
  ])).await;

  codex.submit(Op::UserTurn { ... }).await?;

  // Assert request body if needed.
  let request = mock.single_request();
  // assert using request.function_call_output(call_id) or request.json_body() or other helpers.
  ```

#### app-server integration testing

- Tests should exercise app-server's public JSON-RPC API.
- Use similar server mocking as for core integration tests.
- Use `TestAppServer::builder().build()` and `TestAppServer::send_thread_start_request_with_auto_env()`
  by default to ensure that new tests work with foreign app/exec OSes. See `$remote-tests` for
  details.

## App-server API Development Best Practices

These guidelines apply to app-server protocol work in `codex-rs`, especially:

- `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`
- `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2.rs`
- `app-server/README.md`

### Core Rules

- All active API development should happen in app-server v2. Do not add new API surface area to v1.
- Follow payload naming consistently:
  `*Params` for request payloads, `*Response` for responses, and `*Notification` for notifications.
- Expose RPC methods as `<resource>/<method>` and keep `<resource>` singular (for example, `thread/read`, `app/list`).
- Always expose fields as camelCase on the wire with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` unless a tagged union or explicit compatibility requirement needs a targeted rename.
- Always expose string enum values as camelCase on the wire with matching serde and TS `rename_all = "camelCase"` annotations unless an explicit compatibility requirement needs targeted renames.
- Exception: config RPC payloads are expected to use snake_case to mirror config.toml keys (see the config read/write/list APIs in `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2.rs`).
- Always set `#[ts(export_to = "v2/")]` on v2 request/response/notification types so generated TypeScript lands in the correct namespace.
- Never use `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` for v2 API payload fields.
  Exception: client->server requests that intentionally have no params may use:
  `params: #[ts(type = "undefined")] #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] Option<()>`.
- Keep Rust and TS wire renames aligned. If a field or variant uses `#[serde(rename = "...")]`, add matching `#[ts(rename = "...")]`.
- For discriminated unions, use explicit tagging in both serializers:
  `#[serde(tag = "type", ...)]` and `#[ts(tag = "type", ...)]`.
- Prefer plain `String` IDs at the API boundary (do UUID parsing/conversion internally if needed).
- Timestamps should be integer Unix seconds (`i64`) and named `*_at` (for example, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `resets_at`).
- For experimental API surface area:
  use `#[experimental("method/or/field")]`, derive `ExperimentalApi` when field-level gating is needed, and use `inspect_params: true` in `common.rs` when only some fields of a method are experimental.

### Client->server request payloads (`*Params`)

- Every optional field must be annotated with `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`. Do not use `#[ts(optional = nullable)]` outside client->server request payloads (`*Params`).
- Optional collection fields (for example `Vec`, `HashMap`) must use `Option<...>` + `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`. Do not use `#[serde(default)]` to model optional collections, and do not use `skip_serializing_if` on v2 payload fields.
- When you want omission to mean `false` for boolean fields, use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")] pub field: bool` over `Option<bool>`.
- For new list methods, implement cursor pagination by default:
  request fields `pub cursor: Option<String>` and `pub limit: Option<u32>`,
  response fields `pub data: Vec<...>` and `pub next_cursor: Option<String>`.

### Development Workflow

- Update app-server docs/examples when API behavior changes (at minimum `app-server/README.md`).
- Regenerate schema fixtures when API shapes change:
  `just write-app-server-schema`
  (and `just write-app-server-schema --experimental` when experimental API fixtures are affected).
- Validate with `just test -p codex-app-server-protocol`.
- Avoid boilerplate tests that only assert experimental field markers for individual
  request fields in `common.rs`; rely on schema generation/tests and behavioral coverage instead.

## Python Development Best Practices

### Ignore Python 2 compatibility

This project uses Python 3+. You should not use the `__future__` module.

If you need to worry about feature compatibility between different 3.xx point releases, check the
closest `pyproject.toml`'s `requires-python` field to see what minimum runtime version is supported.

## Platform Support

Tests and features must support Linux, macOS and Windows unless feature is explicitly OS-specific.

Suffice supports running connected app-server and exec-server on different operating systems. See the
`$remote-tests` skill for details about integration testing these configurations.

546:                     debug!("realtime websocket ignored unsupported text frame");
547:                 }
548:                 Message::Close(frame) => {
549:                     self.is_closed.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
550:                     info!(
551:                         "realtime websocket closed: code={:?} reason={:?}",
552:                         frame.as_ref().map(|frame| frame.code),
553:                         frame.as_ref().map(|frame| frame.reason.as_str())
554:                     );
555:                     if self.event_parser != RealtimeEventParser::FramelessBidi {
556:                         return Ok(None);
557:                     }
558:                     return match frame {
559:                         Some(frame) if frame.code == CloseCode::Normal => Ok(None),
560:                         Some(frame) => Err(ApiError::Stream(format!(
561:                             "realtime websocket closed unexpectedly: code={:?} reason={:?}",
562:                             frame.code, frame.reason
563:                         ))),
564:                         None => Err(ApiError::Stream(
565:                             "realtime websocket closed unexpectedly without a status code"
566:                                 .to_string(),
567:                         )),
568:                     };
569:                 }
570:                 Message::Binary(_) => {
571:                     return Ok(Some(RealtimeEvent::Error(
572:                         "unexpected binary realtime websocket event".to_string(),
573:                     )));
574:                 }
575:                 Message::Frame(_) | Message::Ping(_) | Message::Pong(_) => {}
576:             }
577:         }
578:     }
579: 
580:     async fn wait_for_session_started(&self) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
581:         let Some(event) = self.next_event().await? else {
582:             return Err(ApiError::Stream(
583:                 "frameless realtime session ended before session.started".to_string(),
584:             ));
585:         };
586:         match &event {
587:             RealtimeEvent::SessionUpdated { .. } => {
588:                 self.pending_events.lock().await.push_back(event);
589:                 Ok(())
590:             }
591:             RealtimeEvent::Error(message) => Err(ApiError::Stream(message.clone())),
592:             _ => Err(ApiError::Stream(
593:                 "frameless realtime session received an event before session.started".to_string(),
594:             )),
595:         }
596:     }
597: 
598:     async fn update_active_transcript(&self, event: &mut RealtimeEvent) {
599:         let mut active_transcript = self.transcript_state.active.lock().await;
600:         match event {
601:             RealtimeEvent::InputAudioSpeechStarted(_) => {
602:                 active_transcript.new_input_entry = true;
603:             }
604:             RealtimeEvent::InputTranscriptDelta(RealtimeTranscriptDelta { delta, .. }) => {
605:                 let force_new = active_transcript.new_input_entry;
606:                 append_transcript_delta(&mut active_transcript.entries, "user", delta, force_new);
607:                 active_transcript.new_input_entry = false;
608:             }
609:             RealtimeEvent::OutputTranscriptDelta(RealtimeTranscriptDelta { delta, .. }) => {
610:                 let force_new = active_transcript.new_output_entry;
611:                 append_transcript_delta(
612:                     &mut active_transcript.entries,
613:                     "assistant",
614:                     delta,
615:                     force_new,
616:                 );
617:                 active_transcript.new_output_entry = false;
618:             }
619:             RealtimeEvent::InputTranscriptDone(done) => {
620:                 let force_new = active_transcript.new_input_entry;
621:                 apply_transcript_done(
622:                     &mut active_transcript.entries,
623:                     "user",
624:                     &done.text,
625:                     force_new,
626:                 );
627:                 active_transcript.new_input_entry = false;
628:             }
629:             RealtimeEvent::OutputTranscriptDone(done) => {
630:                 let force_new = active_transcript.new_output_entry;
631:                 apply_transcript_done(
632:                     &mut active_transcript.entries,
633:                     "assistant",
634:                     &done.text,
635:                     force_new,
636:                 );
637:                 active_transcript.new_output_entry = false;
638:             }
639:             RealtimeEvent::HandoffRequested(handoff) => {
640:                 append_handoff_input(&mut active_transcript.entries, &handoff.input_transcript);
641:                 handoff.active_transcript = std::mem::take(&mut active_transcript.entries);
642:                 active_transcript.new_input_entry = true;
643:                 active_transcript.new_output_entry = true;
644:             }
645:             RealtimeEvent::ResponseCreated(_) => {
646:                 active_transcript.new_output_entry = true;
647:             }
648:             RealtimeEvent::SessionUpdated { .. }
649:             | RealtimeEvent::AudioOut(_)
650:             | RealtimeEvent::ResponseCancelled(_)
651:             | RealtimeEvent::ResponseDone(_)
652:             | RealtimeEvent::ConversationItemDone { .. }
653:             | RealtimeEvent::NoopRequested(_)
654:             | RealtimeEvent::ConversationItemAdded(_)
655:             | RealtimeEvent::Error(_) => {}
656:         }
657:         truncate_active_transcript(&mut active_transcript.entries);
658:     }
659: }

661: impl RealtimeTranscriptState {
662:     pub async fn take_transcript_tail(&self) -> Vec<RealtimeTranscriptEntry> {
663:         std::mem::take(&mut self.active.lock().await.entries)
664:     }

667: fn truncate_active_transcript(entries: &mut Vec<RealtimeTranscriptEntry>) {
668:     let mut total_bytes = transcript_entries_bytes(entries);
669:     while total_bytes > MAX_ACTIVE_TRANSCRIPT_BYTES && entries.len() > 1 {
670:         total_bytes = total_bytes.saturating_sub(transcript_entry_bytes(&entries[0]));
671:         entries.remove(0);
672:     }
673:     let Some(entry) = entries.first_mut() else {
674:         return;
675:     };
676:     let entry_overhead = entry.role.len() + 3;
677:     let max_text_bytes = MAX_ACTIVE_TRANSCRIPT_BYTES.saturating_sub(entry_overhead);
678:     if entry.text.len() <= max_text_bytes {
679:         return;
680:     }
681:     let mut start = entry
682:         .text
683:         .len()
684:         .saturating_sub(max_text_bytes.saturating_sub(TRUNCATED_TRANSCRIPT_PREFIX.len()));
685:     while !entry.text.is_char_boundary(start) {
686:         start += 1;
687:     }
688:     entry.text = format!("{TRUNCATED_TRANSCRIPT_PREFIX}{}", &entry.text[start..]);
689: }
690: 
691: fn transcript_entries_bytes(entries: &[RealtimeTranscriptEntry]) -> usize {
692:     entries.iter().map(transcript_entry_bytes).sum()
693: }
694: 
695: fn transcript_entry_bytes(entry: &RealtimeTranscriptEntry) -> usize {
696:     entry.role.len() + entry.text.len() + 3
697: }
698: 
699: fn append_transcript_delta(
700:     entries: &mut Vec<RealtimeTranscriptEntry>,
701:     role: &str,
702:     delta: &str,
703:     force_new: bool,
704: ) {
705:     if delta.is_empty() {
706:         return;
707:     }
708: 
709:     if !force_new
710:         && let Some(last_entry) = entries.last_mut()
711:         && last_entry.role == role
712:     {
713:         last_entry.text.push_str(delta);
714:         return;
715:     }
716: 
717:     entries.push(RealtimeTranscriptEntry {
718:         role: role.to_string(),
719:         text: delta.to_string(),
720:     });
721: }
722: 
723: fn apply_transcript_done(
724:     entries: &mut Vec<RealtimeTranscriptEntry>,
725:     role: &str,
726:     text: &str,
727:     force_new: bool,
728: ) {
729:     if text.is_empty() {
730:         return;
731:     }
732: 
733:     if !force_new
734:         && let Some(last_entry) = entries.last_mut()
735:         && last_entry.role == role
736:     {
737:         last_entry.text = text.to_string();
738:         return;
739:     }
740: 
741:     entries.push(RealtimeTranscriptEntry {
742:         role: role.to_string(),
743:         text: text.to_string(),
744:     });
745: }
746: 
747: fn append_handoff_input(entries: &mut Vec<RealtimeTranscriptEntry>, input: &str) {
748:     let input = input.trim();
749:     if input.is_empty() || contains_transcript_entry(entries, "user", input) {
750:         return;
751:     }
752: 
753:     entries.push(RealtimeTranscriptEntry {
754:         role: "user".to_string(),
755:         text: input.to_string(),
756:     });
757: }
758: 
759: fn contains_transcript_entry(entries: &[RealtimeTranscriptEntry], role: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
760:     entries
761:         .iter()
762:         .any(|entry| entry.role == role && entry.text.trim() == text.trim())
763: }

838:         call_id: &str,
839:         extra_headers: HeaderMap,

854:     async fn connect_sideband(
855:         &self,
856:         config: RealtimeSessionConfig,
857:         call_id: &str,
858:         extra_headers: HeaderMap,
859:         default_headers: HeaderMap,
860:         session_initialization: RealtimeSessionInitialization,
861:         transcript_state: RealtimeTranscriptState,
862:     ) -> Result<RealtimeWebsocketConnection, ApiError> {
863:         // The WebRTC call already exists; this loop only retries joining its sideband control
864:         // socket. Once joined, the returned connection is the same reader/writer state that the
865:         // ordinary websocket start path uses.
866:         for attempt in 0..=self.provider.retry.max_attempts {
867:             let result = self
868:                 .connect_webrtc_sideband_once(
869:                     config.clone(),
870:                     call_id,
871:                     extra_headers.clone(),
872:                     default_headers.clone(),
873:                     session_initialization,
874:                     transcript_state.clone(),
875:                 )
876:                 .await;
877:             match result {
878:                 Ok(connection) => return Ok(connection),
879:                 Err(err) if webrtc_sideband_session_ended(&err) => return Err(err),
880:                 Err(err) if attempt < self.provider.retry.max_attempts => {
881:                     let delay = backoff(self.provider.retry.base_delay, attempt + 1);
882:                     warn!(
883:                         attempt = attempt + 1,
884:                         call_id,
885:                         delay_ms = delay.as_millis(),
886:                         "realtime sideband websocket connect failed; retrying: {err}"
887:                     );
888:                     sleep(delay).await;
889:                 }
890:                 Err(err) => return Err(err),
891:             }
892:         }
893: 
894:         Err(ApiError::Stream(
895:             "realtime sideband websocket retry loop exhausted".to_string(),
896:         ))
897:     }

899:     async fn connect_webrtc_sideband_once(
900:         &self,
901:         config: RealtimeSessionConfig,
902:         call_id: &str,
903:         extra_headers: HeaderMap,
904:         default_headers: HeaderMap,
905:         session_initialization: RealtimeSessionInitialization,
906:         transcript_state: RealtimeTranscriptState,
907:     ) -> Result<RealtimeWebsocketConnection, ApiError> {
908:         // Keep the parser/session query shaping from standalone realtime while replacing the model
909:         // query with a call_id join onto an existing WebRTC session.
910:         let ws_url = self.webrtc_sideband_url(config.event_parser, config.session_mode, call_id)?;
911:         self.connect_realtime_websocket_url(
912:             ws_url,
913:             config,
914:             extra_headers,
915:             default_headers,
916:             session_initialization,
917:             transcript_state,
918:         )
919:         .await
920:     }

922:     fn webrtc_sideband_url(
923:         &self,
924:         event_parser: RealtimeEventParser,
925:         session_mode: RealtimeSessionMode,
926:         call_id: &str,
927:     ) -> Result<Url, ApiError> {
928:         websocket_url_from_api_url_for_call(
929:             self.webrtc_sideband_base_url.as_str(),
930:             /*query_params*/ None,
931:             event_parser,
932:             session_mode,
933:             call_id,
934:         )
935:     }

937:     async fn connect_realtime_websocket_url(
938:         &self,
939:         ws_url: Url,
940:         config: RealtimeSessionConfig,
941:         extra_headers: HeaderMap,
942:         default_headers: HeaderMap,
943:         session_initialization: RealtimeSessionInitialization,
944:         transcript_state: RealtimeTranscriptState,
945:     ) -> Result<RealtimeWebsocketConnection, ApiError> {
946:         ensure_rustls_crypto_provider();
947: 
948:         let mut request = ws_url
949:             .as_str()
950:             .into_client_request()
951:             .map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to build websocket request: {err}")))?;
952:         let headers = merge_request_headers(
953:             &self.provider.headers,
954:             with_session_id_header(extra_headers, config.session_id.as_deref())?,
955:             default_headers,
956:         );
957:         request.headers_mut().extend(headers);
958: 
959:         info!("connecting realtime websocket: {ws_url}");
960:         // Realtime websocket TLS should honor the same custom-CA env vars as the rest of Suffice's
961:         // outbound HTTPS and websocket traffic.
962:         let connector = maybe_build_rustls_client_config_with_custom_ca()
963:             .map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to configure websocket TLS: {err}")))?
964:             .map(tokio_tungstenite::Connector::Rustls);
965:         let (stream, response) = tokio_tungstenite::connect_async_tls_with_config(
966:             request,
967:             Some(websocket_config()),
968:             false,
969:             connector,
970:         )
971:         .await
972:         .map_err(map_realtime_websocket_connect_error)?;
973:         info!(
974:             ws_url = %ws_url,
975:             status = %response.status(),
976:             "realtime websocket connected"
977:         );
978: 
979:         let (stream, rx_message) = WsStream::new(stream);
980:         let connection = RealtimeWebsocketConnection::new(
981:             stream,
982:             rx_message,
983:             config.event_parser,
984:             transcript_state,
985:         );
986:         let initialize_session = match session_initialization {
987:             RealtimeSessionInitialization::NewSession => true,
988:             RealtimeSessionInitialization::LegacyWebrtcSideband => {
989:                 config.event_parser != RealtimeEventParser::FramelessBidi
990:             }
991:             RealtimeSessionInitialization::ExistingCall => false,
992:         };
993:         if initialize_session {
994:             debug!(
995:                 session_id = config.session_id.as_deref().unwrap_or("<none>"),
996:                 "realtime websocket sending session.update"
997:             );
998:             connection
999:                 .writer
1000:                 .send_session_update(
1001:                     config.instructions,
1002:                     config.initial_items,
1003:                     config.session_mode,
1004:                     config.output_modality,
1005:                     config.voice,
1006:                     config.delegation_ack_filler,
1007:                 )
1008:                 .await?;
1009:         }
1010:         if matches!(
1011:             session_initialization,
1012:             RealtimeSessionInitialization::NewSession
1013:         ) && config.event_parser == RealtimeEventParser::FramelessBidi
1014:         {
1015:             connection.events.wait_for_session_started().await?;
1016:         }
1017:         Ok(connection)
1018:     }
1019: }

1074: fn websocket_url_from_api_url(
1075:     api_url: &str,
1076:     query_params: Option<&HashMap<String, String>>,
1077:     model: Option<&str>,
1078:     event_parser: RealtimeEventParser,
1079:     _session_mode: RealtimeSessionMode,
1080: ) -> Result<Url, ApiError> {
1081:     let mut url = Url::parse(api_url)
1082:         .map_err(|err| ApiError::Stream(format!("failed to parse realtime api_url: {err}")))?;
1083: 
1084:     normalize_realtime_path(&mut url, event_parser);
1085: 
1086:     match url.scheme() {
1087:         "ws" | "wss" => {}
1088:         "http" | "https" => {
1089:             let scheme = if url.scheme() == "http" { "ws" } else { "wss" };
1090:             let _ = url.set_scheme(scheme);
1091:         }
1092:         scheme => {
1093:             return Err(ApiError::Stream(format!(
1094:                 "unsupported realtime api_url scheme: {scheme}"
1095:             )));
1096:         }
1097:     }
1098: 
1099:     let intent = websocket_intent(event_parser);
1100:     let has_extra_query_params = query_params.is_some_and(|query_params| {
1101:         query_params
1102:             .iter()
1103:             .any(|(key, _)| key != "intent" && !(key == "model" && model.is_some()))
1104:     });
1105:     if intent.is_some() || model.is_some() || has_extra_query_params {
1106:         let mut query = url.query_pairs_mut();
1107:         if let Some(intent) = intent {
1108:             query.append_pair("intent", intent);
1109:         }
1110:         if let Some(model) = model {
1111:             query.append_pair("model", model);
1112:         }
1113:         if let Some(query_params) = query_params {
1114:             for (key, value) in query_params {
1115:                 if key == "intent" || (key == "model" && model.is_some()) {
1116:                     continue;
1117:                 }
1118:                 query.append_pair(key, value);
1119:             }
1120:         }
1121:     }
1122: 
1123:     Ok(url)
1124: }

1126: fn websocket_url_from_api_url_for_call(
1127:     api_url: &str,
1128:     query_params: Option<&HashMap<String, String>>,
1129:     event_parser: RealtimeEventParser,
1130:     session_mode: RealtimeSessionMode,
1131:     call_id: &str,
1132: ) -> Result<Url, ApiError> {
1133:     let mut url = websocket_url_from_api_url(
1134:         api_url,
1135:         query_params,
1136:         /*model*/ None,
1137:         event_parser,
1138:         session_mode,
1139:     )?;
1140:     match event_parser {
1141:         RealtimeEventParser::FramelessBidi => {
1142:             if matches!(call_id, "." | "..") {
1143:                 return Err(ApiError::InvalidRequest {
1144:                     message: format!("invalid realtime call id: {call_id}"),
1145:                 });
1146:             }
1147:             url.path_segments_mut()
1148:                 .map_err(|()| {
1149:                     ApiError::Stream(
1150:                         "realtime sideband URL cannot contain path segments".to_string(),
1151:                     )
1152:                 })?
1153:                 .pop_if_empty()
1154:                 .push(call_id);
1155:         }
1156:         RealtimeEventParser::V1 | RealtimeEventParser::RealtimeV2 => {
1157:             url.query_pairs_mut().append_pair("call_id", call_id);
1158:         }
1159:     }
1160:     Ok(url)
1161: }

1163: fn normalize_realtime_path(url: &mut Url, event_parser: RealtimeEventParser) {
1164:     if event_parser == RealtimeEventParser::FramelessBidi {
1165:         let path = url.path().to_string();
1166:         if path.is_empty() || path == "/" || path == "/v1" || path == "/v1/" {
1167:             url.set_path("/v1/live");
1168:         } else if let Some(prefix) = path.trim_end_matches('/').strip_suffix("/realtime") {
1169:             url.set_path(&format!("{prefix}/live"));
1170:         } else if path.ends_with("/live/") {
1171:             url.set_path(path.trim_end_matches('/'));
1172:         }
1173:         return;
