109: pub(super) fn context_append_chunks(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
110:     if text.len() <= CONTEXT_APPEND_MAX_BYTES {
111:         return vec![text.to_string()];
112:     }
113: 
114:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
115:     let mut start = 0;
116:     while start < text.len() {
117:         let mut end = (start + CONTEXT_APPEND_MAX_BYTES).min(text.len());
118:         while end > start && !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
119:             end -= 1;
120:         }
121:         chunks.push(text[start..end].to_string());
122:         start = end;
123:     }
124:     chunks
125: }

1442:     enum TestRealtimeTermination {
1443:         Close(Option<CloseCode>),
1444:         EventChannelEnd,
1445:     }
1446: 
1447:     async fn realtime_termination_is_transport_error(
1448:         event_parser: RealtimeEventParser,
1449:         termination: TestRealtimeTermination,
1450:     ) -> bool {
1451:         let (tx_message, rx_message) = async_channel::unbounded();
1452:         let events = RealtimeWebsocketEvents {
1453:             rx_message,
1454:             pending_events: Arc::new(Mutex::new(VecDeque::new())),
1455:             transcript_state: RealtimeTranscriptState::default(),
1456:             event_parser,
1457:             is_closed: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
1458:         };
1459:         match termination {
1460:             TestRealtimeTermination::Close(close_code) => {
1461:                 let frame = close_code.map(|code| CloseFrame {
1462:                     code,
1463:                     reason: "session ended".into(),
1464:                 });
1465:                 tx_message
1466:                     .send(Ok(Message::Close(frame)))
1467:                     .await
1468:                     .expect("send close frame");
1469:             }
1470:             TestRealtimeTermination::EventChannelEnd => drop(tx_message),
1471:         }
1472:         events.next_event().await.is_err()
1473:     }

156:         .unwrap_or(call_id)

158:     let arguments = item.get("arguments").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");

160:     Some(RealtimeEvent::HandoffRequested(RealtimeHandoffRequested {
161:         handoff_id: call_id.to_string(),

1: //! Translation from a Responses-shaped request into an OpenAI-compatible
2: //! `/chat/completions` body.
3: //!
4: //! Suffice speaks the Responses API everywhere above this module. Providers that
5: //! only expose Chat Completions (Z.ai/GLM, most OSS servers) get their request
6: //! rewritten here, and their SSE frames rewritten back in `crate::sse::chat`.
7: 
8: use crate::common::ResponsesApiRequest;
9: use codex_protocol::models::ContentItem;
10: use codex_protocol::models::FunctionCallOutputContentItem;
11: use codex_protocol::models::ReasoningItemContent;
12: use codex_protocol::models::ResponseItem;
13: use codex_protocol::openai_models::ReasoningEffort;
14: use serde_json::Value;
15: use serde_json::json;
16: use std::collections::HashMap;
17: 
18: /// Builds the `/chat/completions` request body for `request`.
19: pub(crate) fn chat_body_from_responses_request(request: &ResponsesApiRequest) -> Value {
20:     let mut messages = Vec::<Value>::new();
21:     if !request.instructions.is_empty() {
22:         messages.push(json!({"role": "system", "content": request.instructions}));
23:     }
24: 
25:     let input = request.input.as_slice();
26:     let reasoning_by_anchor_index = anchor_reasoning(input);
27:     let mut last_assistant_text: Option<String> = None;
28: 
29:     for (idx, item) in input.iter().enumerate() {
30:         match item {
31:             ResponseItem::Message { role, content, .. } => {
32:                 let mut text = String::new();
33:                 let mut parts: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
34:                 let mut saw_image = false;
35: 
36:                 for c in content {
37:                     match c {
38:                         ContentItem::InputText { text: t } | ContentItem::OutputText { text: t } => {
39:                             text.push_str(t);
40:                             parts.push(json!({"type": "text", "text": t}));
41:                         }
42:                         ContentItem::InputImage { image_url, .. } => {
43:                             saw_image = true;
44:                             parts.push(json!({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image_url}}));
45:                         }
46:                         // Audio has no Chat Completions equivalent.
47:                         _ => {}
48:                     }
49:                 }
50: 
51:                 // Chat Completions has no notion of duplicate assistant turns;
52:                 // collapsing them keeps the transcript well-formed.
53:                 if role == "assistant" {
54:                     if last_assistant_text.as_ref() == Some(&text) {
55:                         continue;
56:                     }
57:                     last_assistant_text = Some(text.clone());
58:                 }
59: 
60:                 let content_value = if role != "assistant" && saw_image {
61:                     json!(parts)
62:                 } else {
63:                     json!(text)
64:                 };
65: 
66:                 // Chat Completions has no `developer` role, and GLM rejects the
67:                 // whole request with error 1214 rather than ignoring it. The
68:                 // role was introduced as a rename of `system`, so map it back.
69:                 let chat_role = if role == "developer" {
70:                     "system"
71:                 } else {
72:                     role.as_str()
73:                 };
74:                 let mut msg = json!({"role": chat_role, "content": content_value});
75:                 if role == "assistant"
76:                     && let Some(reasoning) = reasoning_by_anchor_index.get(&idx)
77:                     && let Some(obj) = msg.as_object_mut()
78:                 {
79:                     obj.insert("reasoning_content".to_string(), json!(reasoning));
80:                 }
81:                 messages.push(msg);
82:             }
83:             ResponseItem::FunctionCall {
84:                 name,
85:                 arguments,
86:                 call_id,
87:                 ..
88:             } => {
89:                 push_tool_call(
90:                     &mut messages,
91:                     json!({
92:                         "id": call_id,
93:                         "type": "function",
94:                         "function": {"name": name, "arguments": arguments},
95:                     }),
96:                     reasoning_by_anchor_index.get(&idx).map(String::as_str),
97:                 );
98:             }
99:             ResponseItem::FunctionCallOutput { call_id, output, .. } => {
100:                 let content_value = match output.content_items() {
101:                     Some(items) => json!(
102:                         items
103:                             .iter()
104:                             .filter_map(|it| match it {
105:                                 FunctionCallOutputContentItem::InputText { text } => {
106:                                     Some(json!({"type": "text", "text": text}))
107:                                 }
108:                                 FunctionCallOutputContentItem::InputImage { image_url, .. } => {
109:                                     Some(json!({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image_url}}))
110:                                 }
111:                                 _ => None,
112:                             })
113:                             .collect::<Vec<_>>()
114:                     ),
115:                     None => json!(output.text_content().unwrap_or_default()),
116:                 };
117:                 messages.push(json!({
118:                     "role": "tool",
119:                     "tool_call_id": call_id,
120:                     "content": content_value,
121:                 }));
122:             }
123:             ResponseItem::CustomToolCall {
124:                 call_id,
125:                 name,
126:                 input,
127:                 ..
128:             } => {
129:                 push_tool_call(
130:                     &mut messages,
131:                     json!({
132:                         "id": call_id,
133:                         "type": "function",
134:                         "function": {"name": name, "arguments": input},
135:                     }),
136:                     reasoning_by_anchor_index.get(&idx).map(String::as_str),
137:                 );
138:             }
139:             ResponseItem::CustomToolCallOutput {
140:                 call_id, output, ..
141:             } => {
142:                 messages.push(json!({
143:                     "role": "tool",
144:                     "tool_call_id": call_id,
145:                     "content": output,
146:                 }));
147:             }
148:             // Reasoning is folded into its anchor message above; everything else
149:             // has no Chat Completions representation.
150:             _ => continue,
151:         }
152:     }
153: 
154:     let mut body = json!({
155:         "model": request.model,
156:         "messages": messages,
157:         "stream": true,
158:         // Without this the provider omits `usage`, and Suffice cannot track cost
159:         // or drive the auto-compaction trigger.
160:         "stream_options": {"include_usage": true},
161:     });
162: 
163:     let Some(obj) = body.as_object_mut() else {
164:         return body;
165:     };
166: 
167:     if let Some(tools) = request.tools.as_ref().map(chat_tools_from_responses_tools)
168:         && !tools.is_empty()
169:     {
170:         obj.insert("tools".to_string(), json!(tools));
171:         obj.insert("tool_choice".to_string(), json!(request.tool_choice));
172:         obj.insert(
173:             "parallel_tool_calls".to_string(),
174:             json!(request.parallel_tool_calls),
175:         );
176:     }
177: 
178:     // Z.ai/GLM gate chain-of-thought behind `thinking` rather than `reasoning`.
179:     // GLM-5.3 rejects `{"type": "disabled"}` outright, so enabled is the only value
180:     // worth sending; depth is chosen with `reasoning_effort` instead.
181:     if let Some(reasoning) = request.reasoning.as_ref() {
182:         obj.insert("thinking".to_string(), json!({"type": "enabled"}));
183:         if let Some(effort) = reasoning.effort.as_ref() {
184:             obj.insert(
185:                 "reasoning_effort".to_string(),
186:                 json!(glm_reasoning_effort(effort)),
187:             );
188:         }
189:     }
190: 
191:     if let Some(text) = request.text.as_ref()
192:         && let Ok(Value::Object(text)) = serde_json::to_value(text)
193:         && let Some(format) = text.get("format")
194:     {
195:         obj.insert("response_format".to_string(), format.clone());
196:     }
197: 
198:     body
199: }

201: /// Projects Suffice's effort ladder onto the three rungs GLM-5.3 accepts.
202: ///
203: /// `low`, `high` and `max` are the only legal values; anything else is rejected outright,
204: /// and omitting the field entirely silently selects `max`, the most expensive rung. So a
205: /// config still carrying an effort written for another provider must be clamped rather than
206: /// forwarded or dropped. Clamping at the wire boundary leaves the rest of Suffice free to keep
207: /// its own wider ladder.
208: fn glm_reasoning_effort(effort: &ReasoningEffort) -> &'static str {
209:     match effort {
210:         ReasoningEffort::None | ReasoningEffort::Minimal | ReasoningEffort::Low => "low",
211:         ReasoningEffort::Medium | ReasoningEffort::High => "high",
212:         ReasoningEffort::XHigh | ReasoningEffort::Max | ReasoningEffort::Ultra => "max",
213:         // Rungs with no depth ordering to project. `high` is the model default here, and the
214:         // cheaper of the two rungs the picker offers without an explicit detour.
215:         ReasoningEffort::Persistent | ReasoningEffort::Custom(_) => "high",
216:     }
217: }

219: /// Rewrites Responses tool specs (`{type, name, parameters}`) into the nested
220: /// Chat Completions shape (`{type, function: {name, parameters}}`).
221: fn chat_tools_from_responses_tools(tools: &crate::common::ResponsesApiTools) -> Vec<Value> {
222:     let Ok(Value::Array(tools)) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(tools.as_raw_value().get()) else {
223:         return Vec::new();
224:     };
225: 
226:     tools
227:         .into_iter()
228:         .filter_map(|tool| {
229:             let obj = tool.as_object()?;
230:             // Provider-native tools (web_search, local_shell, ...) have no
231:             // Chat Completions equivalent; dropping them is better than sending
232:             // a body the provider will reject outright.
233:             if obj.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("function") {
234:                 return None;
235:             }
236:             // Already nested (some callers hand us Chat-shaped specs).
237:             if obj.contains_key("function") {
238:                 return Some(tool);
239:             }
240: 
241:             let mut function = serde_json::Map::new();
242:             for key in ["name", "description", "parameters", "strict"] {
243:                 if let Some(value) = obj.get(key) {
244:                     function.insert(key.to_string(), value.clone());
245:                 }
246:             }
247:             Some(json!({"type": "function", "function": function}))
248:         })
249:         .collect()
250: }

252: /// Attaches each `Reasoning` item to the assistant message or tool call it belongs
253: /// to, so it can ride along as `reasoning_content`.
254: ///
255: /// Every reasoning item still present in `input` is carried. Which reasoning survives
256: /// a finished turn is decided in history, where the size of the reasoning can be
257: /// weighed against the prompt-cache invalidation that removing it costs. Dropping more
258: /// of it here would rewrite the messages history deliberately left alone, and cost
259: /// exactly the cache miss that decision was made to avoid.
260: fn anchor_reasoning(input: &[ResponseItem]) -> HashMap<usize, String> {
261:     let mut anchored: HashMap<usize, String> = HashMap::new();
262: 
263:     for (idx, item) in input.iter().enumerate() {
264:         let ResponseItem::Reasoning {
265:             content: Some(items),
266:             ..
267:         } = item
268:         else {
269:             continue;
270:         };
271: 
272:         let mut text = String::new();
273:         for entry in items {
274:             match entry {
275:                 ReasoningItemContent::ReasoningText { text: segment }
276:                 | ReasoningItemContent::Text { text: segment } => text.push_str(segment),
277:             }
278:         }
279:         if text.trim().is_empty() {
280:             continue;
281:         }
282: 
283:         // Reasoning precedes the item it explains, but a provider may also emit
284:         // it right after an assistant message. Prefer the following item.
285:         let anchor = input
286:             .get(idx + 1)
287:             .and_then(|next| match next {
288:                 ResponseItem::FunctionCall { .. } | ResponseItem::CustomToolCall { .. } => {
289:                     Some(idx + 1)
290:                 }
291:                 ResponseItem::Message { role, .. } if role == "assistant" => Some(idx + 1),
292:                 _ => None,
293:             })
294:             .or_else(|| match idx.checked_sub(1).map(|prev| (prev, &input[prev])) {
295:                 Some((prev, ResponseItem::Message { role, .. })) if role == "assistant" => {
296:                     Some(prev)
297:                 }
298:                 _ => None,
299:             });
300: 
301:         if let Some(anchor) = anchor {
302:             anchored
303:                 .entry(anchor)
304:                 .and_modify(|existing| {
305:                     existing.push('\n');
306:                     existing.push_str(&text);
307:                 })
308:                 .or_insert(text);
309:         }
310:     }
311: 
312:     anchored
313: }

315: /// Chat Completions requires consecutive tool calls to be grouped into one
316: /// assistant message carrying `tool_calls: [...]`, followed by the `tool` replies.
317: fn push_tool_call(messages: &mut Vec<Value>, tool_call: Value, reasoning: Option<&str>) {
318:     if let Some(Value::Object(obj)) = messages.last_mut()
319:         && obj.get("role").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("assistant")
320:         && obj.get("content").is_some_and(Value::is_null)
321:         && let Some(tool_calls) = obj.get_mut("tool_calls").and_then(Value::as_array_mut)
322:     {
323:         tool_calls.push(tool_call);
324:         if let Some(reasoning) = reasoning {
325:             match obj.get_mut("reasoning_content") {
326:                 Some(Value::String(existing)) => {
327:                     existing.push('\n');
328:                     existing.push_str(reasoning);
329:                 }
330:                 _ => {
331:                     obj.insert("reasoning_content".to_string(), json!(reasoning));
332:                 }
333:             }
334:         }
335:         return;
336:     }
337: 
338:     let mut msg = json!({
339:         "role": "assistant",
340:         "content": null,
341:         "tool_calls": [tool_call],
342:     });
343:     if let Some(reasoning) = reasoning
344:         && let Some(obj) = msg.as_object_mut()
345:     {
346:         obj.insert("reasoning_content".to_string(), json!(reasoning));
347:     }
348:     messages.push(msg);
349: }

1: //! Translation of OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` SSE frames into the
2: //! Responses-shaped [`ResponseEvent`] stream the rest of Suffice consumes.
3: //!
4: //! See `crate::requests::chat` for the outbound half of the bridge.
5: 
6: use crate::common::ResponseEvent;
7: use crate::common::ResponseStream;
8: use crate::error::ApiError;
9: use crate::telemetry::SseTelemetry;
10: use codex_client::StreamResponse;
11: use codex_protocol::models::ContentItem;
12: use codex_protocol::models::ReasoningItemContent;
13: use codex_protocol::models::ResponseItem;
14: use codex_protocol::protocol::TokenUsage;
15: use eventsource_stream::Eventsource;
16: use futures::Stream;
17: use futures::StreamExt;
18: use serde_json::Value;
19: use std::collections::HashMap;
20: use std::sync::Arc;
21: use std::time::Duration;

28: const REQUEST_ID_HEADER: &str = "x-request-id";
29: 
30: pub(crate) fn spawn_chat_stream(
31:     stream_response: StreamResponse,
32:     idle_timeout: Duration,
33:     telemetry: Option<Arc<dyn SseTelemetry>>,
34: ) -> ResponseStream {
35:     let upstream_request_id = stream_response
36:         .headers
37:         .get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER)
38:         .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
39:         .map(str::to_string);
40: 
41:     let (tx_event, rx_event) = mpsc::channel::<Result<ResponseEvent, ApiError>>(1600);
42:     tokio::spawn(async move {
43:         process_chat_sse(stream_response.bytes, tx_event, idle_timeout, telemetry).await;
44:     });
45: 
46:     ResponseStream {
47:         rx_event,
48:         upstream_request_id,
49:     }
50: }

52: #[derive(Default, Debug)]
53: struct ToolCallState {
54:     id: Option<String>,
55:     name: Option<String>,
56:     arguments: String,
57: }
58: 
59: /// Accumulates the in-flight assistant turn while chunks arrive.
60: ///
61: /// Chat Completions streams deltas with no item identity, so we rebuild whole
62: /// `ResponseItem`s here and emit them as `OutputItemDone` at the finish boundary.
63: #[derive(Default)]
64: struct ChatTurn {
65:     assistant: Option<ResponseItem>,
66:     reasoning: Option<ResponseItem>,
67:     tool_calls: HashMap<usize, ToolCallState>,
68:     tool_call_order: Vec<usize>,
69:     tool_call_index_by_id: HashMap<String, usize>,
70:     next_tool_call_index: usize,
71:     last_tool_call_index: Option<usize>,
72:     response_id: String,
73:     token_usage: Option<TokenUsage>,
74:     end_turn: Option<bool>,
75: }
76: 
77: pub(crate) async fn process_chat_sse<S>(
78:     stream: S,
79:     tx_event: mpsc::Sender<Result<ResponseEvent, ApiError>>,
80:     idle_timeout: Duration,
81:     telemetry: Option<Arc<dyn SseTelemetry>>,
82: ) where
83:     S: Stream<Item = Result<bytes::Bytes, codex_client::TransportError>> + Unpin,
84: {
85:     let mut stream = stream.eventsource();
86:     let mut turn = ChatTurn::default();
87:     let _ = tx_event.send(Ok(ResponseEvent::Created)).await;
88: 
89:     loop {
90:         let start = Instant::now();
91:         let response = timeout(idle_timeout, stream.next()).await;
92:         if let Some(t) = telemetry.as_ref() {
93:             t.on_sse_poll(&response, start.elapsed());
94:         }
95: 
96:         let sse = match response {
97:             Ok(Some(Ok(sse))) => sse,
98:             Ok(Some(Err(e))) => {
99:                 let _ = tx_event.send(Err(ApiError::Stream(e.to_string()))).await;
100:                 return;
101:             }
102:             Ok(None) => {
103:                 complete(&tx_event, &mut turn).await;
104:                 return;
105:             }
106:             Err(_) => {
107:                 let _ = tx_event
108:                     .send(Err(ApiError::Stream("idle timeout waiting for SSE".into())))
109:                     .await;
110:                 return;
111:             }
112:         };
113: 
114:         trace!("chat SSE event: {}", sse.data);
115:         let data = sse.data.trim();
116:         if data.is_empty() {
117:             continue;
118:         }
119:         if data == "[DONE]" || data == "DONE" {
120:             complete(&tx_event, &mut turn).await;
121:             return;
122:         }
123: 
124:         let value: Value = match serde_json::from_str(data) {
125:             Ok(value) => value,
126:             Err(err) => {
127:                 debug!("failed to parse chat completions SSE event: {err}, data: {data}");
128:                 continue;
129:             }
130:         };
131: 
132:         if let Some(error) = value.get("error") {
133:             let message = error
134:                 .get("message")
135:                 .and_then(Value::as_str)
136:                 .unwrap_or("chat completions stream returned an error");
137:             let _ = tx_event
138:                 .send(Err(ApiError::Stream(message.to_string())))
139:                 .await;
140:             return;
141:         }
142: 
143:         if let Some(id) = value.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str)
144:             && turn.response_id.is_empty()
145:         {
146:             turn.response_id = id.to_string();
147:         }
148: 
149:         // The final `include_usage` chunk carries usage with an empty `choices`.
150:         if let Some(usage) = value.get("usage").filter(|usage| !usage.is_null()) {
151:             turn.token_usage = Some(token_usage_from_chat_usage(usage));
152:         }
153: 
154:         let Some(choices) = value.get("choices").and_then(Value::as_array) else {
155:             continue;
156:         };
157: 
158:         for choice in choices {
159:             if let Some(delta) = choice.get("delta") {
160:                 if let Some(text) = reasoning_text(delta) {
161:                     append_reasoning(&tx_event, &mut turn.reasoning, text).await;
162:                 }
163:                 if let Some(content) = delta.get("content") {
164:                     for text in content_texts(content) {
165:                         append_assistant(&tx_event, &mut turn.assistant, text).await;
166:                     }
167:                 }
168:                 if let Some(tool_calls) = delta.get("tool_calls").and_then(Value::as_array) {
169:                     for tool_call in tool_calls {
170:                         accumulate_tool_call(&mut turn, tool_call);
171:                     }
172:                 }
173:             }
174: 
175:             // Non-streaming-shaped replies still land here for some providers.
176:             if let Some(message) = choice.get("message") {
177:                 if let Some(text) = reasoning_text(message) {
178:                     append_reasoning(&tx_event, &mut turn.reasoning, text).await;
179:                 }
180:                 if let Some(content) = message.get("content") {
181:                     for text in content_texts(content) {
182:                         append_assistant(&tx_event, &mut turn.assistant, text).await;
183:                     }
184:                 }
185:             }
186: 
187:             match choice.get("finish_reason").and_then(Value::as_str) {
188:                 Some("length") => {
189:                     let _ = tx_event.send(Err(ApiError::ContextWindowExceeded)).await;
190:                     return;
191:                 }
192:                 Some("tool_calls") => {
193:                     turn.end_turn = Some(false);
194:                     flush_items(&tx_event, &mut turn).await;
195:                 }
196:                 Some(_) => {
197:                     turn.end_turn = Some(true);
198:                     flush_items(&tx_event, &mut turn).await;
199:                 }
200:                 None => {}
201:             }
202:         }
203:     }
204: }

206: /// Emits the accumulated reasoning, assistant message, and tool calls in the
207: /// order the Responses API would have produced them.
208: async fn flush_items(tx_event: &mpsc::Sender<Result<ResponseEvent, ApiError>>, turn: &mut ChatTurn) {
209:     if let Some(reasoning) = turn.reasoning.take() {
210:         let _ = tx_event
211:             .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::OutputItemDone(reasoning)))
212:             .await;
213:     }
214:     if let Some(assistant) = turn.assistant.take() {
215:         let _ = tx_event
216:             .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::OutputItemDone(assistant)))
217:             .await;
218:     }
219: 
220:     for index in std::mem::take(&mut turn.tool_call_order) {
221:         let Some(state) = turn.tool_calls.remove(&index) else {
222:             continue;
223:         };
224:         let Some(name) = state.name else {
225:             debug!("skipping tool call at index {index}: no function name in stream");
226:             continue;
227:         };
228:         let _ = tx_event
229:             .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::OutputItemDone(ResponseItem::FunctionCall {
230:                 id: None,
231:                 name,
232:                 namespace: None,
233:                 arguments: state.arguments,
234:                 encrypted_function_args: None,
235:                 call_id: state.id.unwrap_or_else(|| format!("tool-call-{index}")),
236:                 internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough: None,
237:             })))
238:             .await;
239:     }
240: }
241: 
242: /// Flushes anything still buffered and closes the turn.
243: ///
244: /// Deferred until `[DONE]` (or stream end) because the usage chunk arrives after
245: /// `finish_reason`, and dropping it would leave Suffice blind to token cost.
246: async fn complete(tx_event: &mpsc::Sender<Result<ResponseEvent, ApiError>>, turn: &mut ChatTurn) {
247:     flush_items(tx_event, turn).await;
248:     let _ = tx_event
249:         .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::Completed {
250:             response_id: std::mem::take(&mut turn.response_id),
251:             token_usage: turn.token_usage.take(),
252:             usage_metadata: None,
253:             end_turn: turn.end_turn,
254:         }))
255:         .await;
256: }

258: fn accumulate_tool_call(turn: &mut ChatTurn, tool_call: &Value) {
259:     let call_id = tool_call.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str);
260: 
261:     // Prefer an index we already associated with this id; providers are
262:     // inconsistent about repeating `index` on continuation frames.
263:     let index = call_id
264:         .and_then(|id| turn.tool_call_index_by_id.get(id).copied())
265:         .or_else(|| {
266:             tool_call
267:                 .get("index")
268:                 .and_then(Value::as_u64)
269:                 .map(|i| i as usize)
270:         })
271:         .or(if call_id.is_none() {
272:             turn.last_tool_call_index
273:         } else {
274:             None
275:         })
276:         .unwrap_or_else(|| {
277:             while turn.tool_calls.contains_key(&turn.next_tool_call_index) {
278:                 turn.next_tool_call_index += 1;
279:             }
280:             let index = turn.next_tool_call_index;
281:             turn.next_tool_call_index += 1;
282:             index
283:         });
284: 
285:     if !turn.tool_calls.contains_key(&index) {
286:         turn.tool_call_order.push(index);
287:     }
288:     let state = turn.tool_calls.entry(index).or_default();
289: 
290:     if let Some(id) = call_id {
291:         state.id.get_or_insert_with(|| id.to_string());
292:         turn.tool_call_index_by_id
293:             .entry(id.to_string())
294:             .or_insert(index);
295:     }
296: 
297:     if let Some(function) = tool_call.get("function") {
298:         if let Some(name) = function.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str)
299:             && !name.is_empty()
300:         {
301:             state.name.get_or_insert_with(|| name.to_string());
302:         }
303:         if let Some(arguments) = function.get("arguments").and_then(Value::as_str) {
304:             state.arguments.push_str(arguments);
305:         }
306:     }
307: 
308:     turn.last_tool_call_index = Some(index);
309: }

311: /// Reads chain-of-thought text from a delta or message.
312: ///
313: /// `reasoning_content` is the Z.ai/GLM spelling; `reasoning` is what other
314: /// OpenAI-compatible servers use, as a string or as `{text}`/`{content}`.
315: fn reasoning_text(node: &Value) -> Option<String> {
316:     if let Some(text) = node.get("reasoning_content").and_then(Value::as_str)
317:         && !text.is_empty()
318:     {
319:         return Some(text.to_string());
320:     }
321: 
322:     let reasoning = node.get("reasoning")?;
323:     let text = reasoning
324:         .as_str()
325:         .or_else(|| reasoning.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str))
326:         .or_else(|| reasoning.get("content").and_then(Value::as_str))?;
327:     (!text.is_empty()).then(|| text.to_string())
328: }
329: 
330: fn content_texts(content: &Value) -> Vec<String> {
331:     match content {
332:         Value::String(text) if !text.is_empty() => vec![text.clone()],
333:         Value::Array(items) => items
334:             .iter()
335:             .filter_map(|item| item.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str))
336:             .filter(|text| !text.is_empty())
337:             .map(str::to_string)
338:             .collect(),
339:         _ => Vec::new(),
340:     }
341: }

370: async fn append_reasoning(
371:     tx_event: &mpsc::Sender<Result<ResponseEvent, ApiError>>,
372:     reasoning: &mut Option<ResponseItem>,
373:     text: String,
374: ) {

377:             id: None,

379:             content: Some(Vec::new()),
380:             encrypted_content: None,

383:         *reasoning = Some(item.clone());
384:         let _ = tx_event
385:             .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::OutputItemAdded(item)))

389:     if let Some(ResponseItem::Reasoning {
390:         content: Some(content),
391:         ..
392:     }) = reasoning
393:     {
394:         let content_index = content.len() as i64;
395:         content.push(ReasoningItemContent::ReasoningText { text: text.clone() });
396:         let _ = tx_event
397:             .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::ReasoningContentDelta {
398:                 delta: text,
399:                 content_index,
400:             }))
401:             .await;
402:     }
403: }

405: fn token_usage_from_chat_usage(usage: &Value) -> TokenUsage {
406:     let field = |name: &str| usage.get(name).and_then(Value::as_i64).unwrap_or(0);
407:     let nested = |parent: &str, name: &str| {
408:         usage
409:             .get(parent)
410:             .and_then(|details| details.get(name))
411:             .and_then(Value::as_i64)
412:             .unwrap_or(0)
413:     };
414: 
415:     let input_tokens = field("prompt_tokens");
416:     let output_tokens = field("completion_tokens");
417:     let total_tokens = match field("total_tokens") {
418:         0 => input_tokens + output_tokens,
419:         total => total,
420:     };
421: 
422:     TokenUsage {
423:         input_tokens,
424:         cached_input_tokens: nested("prompt_tokens_details", "cached_tokens"),
425:         cache_write_input_tokens: 0,
426:         output_tokens,
427:         reasoning_output_tokens: nested("completion_tokens_details", "reasoning_tokens"),
428:         total_tokens,
429:         codex_rollout_budget_units: None,
430:     }
431: }

546: ) {

548:         stream,

557: async fn process_sse_with_treatment(
558:     stream: ByteStream,
559:     tx_event: mpsc::Sender<Result<ResponseEvent, ApiError>>,
560:     idle_timeout: Duration,
561:     telemetry: Option<Arc<dyn SseTelemetry>>,
562:     safety_buffering_treatment: SafetyBufferingTreatment,
563: ) {
564:     let mut stream = stream.eventsource();
565:     let mut response_error: Option<ApiError> = None;
566:     let mut last_server_model: Option<String> = None;
567: 
568:     loop {
569:         let start = Instant::now();
570:         let response = timeout(idle_timeout, stream.next()).await;
571:         if let Some(t) = telemetry.as_ref() {
572:             t.on_sse_poll(&response, start.elapsed());
573:         }
574:         let sse = match response {
575:             Ok(Some(Ok(sse))) => sse,
576:             Ok(Some(Err(e))) => {
577:                 debug!("SSE Error: {e:#}");
578:                 let _ = tx_event.send(Err(ApiError::Stream(e.to_string()))).await;
579:                 return;
580:             }
581:             Ok(None) => {
582:                 let error = response_error.unwrap_or(ApiError::Stream(
583:                     "stream closed before response.completed".into(),
584:                 ));
585:                 let _ = tx_event.send(Err(error)).await;
586:                 return;
587:             }
588:             Err(_) => {
589:                 let _ = tx_event
590:                     .send(Err(ApiError::Stream("idle timeout waiting for SSE".into())))
591:                     .await;
592:                 return;
593:             }
594:         };
595: 
596:         trace!("SSE event: {}", &sse.data);
597: 
598:         let event: ResponsesStreamEvent = match serde_json::from_str(&sse.data) {
599:             Ok(event) => event,
600:             Err(e) => {
601:                 debug!(
602:                     error_category = ?e.classify(),
603:                     error_line = e.line(),
604:                     error_column = e.column(),
605:                     payload_bytes = sse.data.len(),
606:                     "Failed to parse SSE event"
607:                 );
608:                 continue;
609:             }
610:         };
611:         let model_verifications = event.model_verifications();
612:         let turn_moderation_metadata = event.turn_moderation_metadata();
613:         let safety_buffering = event.safety_buffering(&safety_buffering_treatment);
614: 
615:         if let Some(model) = event.response_model()
616:             && last_server_model.as_deref() != Some(model.as_str())
617:         {
618:             if tx_event
619:                 .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::ServerModel(model.clone())))
620:                 .await
621:                 .is_err()
622:             {
623:                 return;
624:             }
625:             last_server_model = Some(model);
626:         }
627:         if let Some(verifications) = model_verifications
628:             && tx_event
629:                 .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::ModelVerifications(verifications)))
630:                 .await
631:                 .is_err()
632:         {
633:             return;
634:         }
635:         if let Some(metadata) = turn_moderation_metadata
636:             && tx_event
637:                 .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::TurnModerationMetadata(metadata)))
638:                 .await
639:                 .is_err()
640:         {
641:             return;
642:         }
643:         if let Some(buffering) = safety_buffering
644:             && tx_event
645:                 .send(Ok(ResponseEvent::SafetyBuffering(buffering)))
646:                 .await
647:                 .is_err()
648:         {
649:             return;
650:         }
651: 
652:         match process_responses_event(event) {
653:             Ok(Some(event)) => {
654:                 let is_completed = matches!(event, ResponseEvent::Completed { .. });
655:                 if tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await.is_err() {
656:                     return;
657:                 }
658:                 if is_completed {
659:                     return;
660:                 }
661:             }
662:             Ok(None) => {}
663:             Err(error) => {
664:                 response_error = Some(error.into_api_error());
665:             }
666:         };
667:     }
668: }

670: fn try_parse_retry_after(err: &Error) -> Option<Duration> {
671:     if err.code.as_deref() != Some("rate_limit_exceeded") {
672:         return None;
673:     }
674: 
675:     let re = rate_limit_regex();
676:     if let Some(message) = &err.message
677:         && let Some(captures) = re.captures(message)
678:     {
679:         let seconds = captures.get(1);
680:         let unit = captures.get(2);
681: 
682:         if let (Some(value), Some(unit)) = (seconds, unit) {
683:             let value = value.as_str().parse::<f64>().ok()?;
684:             let unit = unit.as_str().to_ascii_lowercase();
685: 
686:             if unit == "s" || unit.starts_with("second") {
687:                 return Some(Duration::from_secs_f64(value));
688:             } else if unit == "ms" {
689:                 return Some(Duration::from_millis(value as u64));
690:             }
691:         }
692:     }
693:     None
694: }

696: fn is_context_window_error(error: &Error) -> bool {
697:     error.code.as_deref() == Some("context_length_exceeded")
698: }

700: fn is_quota_exceeded_error(error: &Error) -> bool {
701:     error.code.as_deref() == Some("insufficient_quota")
702: }

704: fn is_usage_not_included(error: &Error) -> bool {
705:     error.code.as_deref() == Some("usage_not_included")
706: }

708: fn is_cyber_policy_error(error: &Error) -> bool {
709:     error.code.as_deref() == Some("cyber_policy")

712: fn is_server_overloaded_error(error: &Error) -> bool {
713:     error.code.as_deref() == Some("server_is_overloaded")
714:         || error.code.as_deref() == Some("slow_down")
715: }

717: fn cyber_policy_fallback_message() -> String {
718:     "This request has been flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.".to_string()
719: }

721: fn cyber_policy_message(message: Option<String>) -> String {
722:     message
723:         .filter(|message| !message.trim().is_empty())
724:         .unwrap_or_else(cyber_policy_fallback_message)
725: }

727: fn rate_limit_regex() -> &'static regex_lite::Regex {
728:     static RE: std::sync::OnceLock<regex_lite::Regex> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
729:     #[expect(clippy::unwrap_used)]
730:     RE.get_or_init(|| {
731:         regex_lite::Regex::new(r"(?i)try again in\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(s|ms|seconds?)").unwrap()
732:     })
733: }

  ```rust
  let request = mock.single_request();
  // assert using request.function_call_output(call_id) or request.json_body() or other helpers.
  ```

#### app-server integration testing

- Tests should exercise app-server's public JSON-RPC API.
- Use similar server mocking as for core integration tests.
- Use `TestAppServer::builder().build()` and `TestAppServer::send_thread_start_request_with_auto_env()`
  by default to ensure that new tests work with foreign app/exec OSes. See `$remote-tests` for
  details.

## App-server API Development Best Practices

These guidelines apply to app-server protocol work in `codex-rs`, especially:

- `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`
- `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2.rs`
- `app-server/README.md`

### Core Rules

- All active API development should happen in app-server v2. Do not add new API surface area to v1.
- Follow payload naming consistently:
  `*Params` for request payloads, `*Response` for responses, and `*Notification` for notifications.
- Expose RPC methods as `<resource>/<method>` and keep `<resource>` singular (for example, `thread/read`, `app/list`).
- Always expose fields as camelCase on the wire with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` unless a tagged union or explicit compatibility requirement needs a targeted rename.
- Always expose string enum values as camelCase on the wire with matching serde and TS `rename_all = "camelCase"` annotations unless an explicit compatibility requirement needs targeted renames.
- Exception: config RPC payloads are expected to use snake_case to mirror config.toml keys (see the config read/write/list APIs in `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2.rs`).
- Always set `#[ts(export_to = "v2/")]` on v2 request/response/notification types so generated TypeScript lands in the correct namespace.
- Never use `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` for v2 API payload fields.
  Exception: client->server requests that intentionally have no params may use:
  `params: #[ts(type = "undefined")] #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] Option<()>`.
- Keep Rust and TS wire renames aligned. If a field or variant uses `#[serde(rename = "...")]`, add matching `#[ts(rename = "...")]`.
- For discriminated unions, use explicit tagging in both serializers:
  `#[serde(tag = "type", ...)]` and `#[ts(tag = "type", ...)]`.
- Prefer plain `String` IDs at the API boundary (do UUID parsing/conversion internally if needed).
- Timestamps should be integer Unix seconds (`i64`) and named `*_at` (for example, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `resets_at`).
- For experimental API surface area:
  use `#[experimental("method/or/field")]`, derive `ExperimentalApi` when field-level gating is needed, and use `inspect_params: true` in `common.rs` when only some fields of a method are experimental.

### Client->server request payloads (`*Params`)

- Every optional field must be annotated with `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`. Do not use `#[ts(optional = nullable)]` outside client->server request payloads (`*Params`).
- Optional collection fields (for example `Vec`, `HashMap`) must use `Option<...>` + `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`. Do not use `#[serde(default)]` to model optional collections, and do not use `skip_serializing_if` on v2 payload fields.
- When you want omission to mean `false` for boolean fields, use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")] pub field: bool` over `Option<bool>`.
- For new list methods, implement cursor pagination by default:
  request fields `pub cursor: Option<String>` and `pub limit: Option<u32>`,
  response fields `pub data: Vec<...>` and `pub next_cursor: Option<String>`.

### Development Workflow

- Update app-server docs/examples when API behavior changes (at minimum `app-server/README.md`).
- Regenerate schema fixtures when API shapes change:
  `just write-app-server-schema`
  (and `just write-app-server-schema --experimental` when experimental API fixtures are affected).
- Validate with `just test -p codex-app-server-protocol`.
- Avoid boilerplate tests that only assert experimental field markers for individual
  request fields in `common.rs`; rely on schema generation/tests and behavioral coverage instead.

## Python Development Best Practices

### Ignore Python 2 compatibility

This project uses Python 3+. You should not use the `__future__` module.

If you need to worry about feature compatibility between different 3.xx point releases, check the
closest `pyproject.toml`'s `requires-python` field to see what minimum runtime version is supported.

## Platform Support

Tests and features must support Linux, macOS and Windows unless feature is explicitly OS-specific.

Suffice supports running connected app-server and exec-server on different operating systems. See the
`$remote-tests` skill for details about integration testing these configurations.

## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `C:/Users/Bedirhan/.suffice-par/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Suffice should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Suffice models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Suffice—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Suffice comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Suffice. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Suffice with a required `.suffice-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Suffice needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Suffice skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Suffice skills into $SUFFICE_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + short path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths after expanding the matching alias from `### Skill roots`.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, the main agent must expand the listed short `path` with the matching alias from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions. If a read is truncated or paginated, continue until EOF.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the directory containing that expanded `SKILL.md` first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, use its routing instructions to identify the files required for the task. The main agent must read each required instruction or reference file itself before acting on it. Do not delegate reading, summarizing, or interpreting skill instructions to a subagent. Subagents may still perform task work when the selected skill allows it.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Progressive disclosure applies to selecting relevant files, not partially reading a selected instruction file. Do not load unrelated references, scripts, or assets.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.
